evidence_policy: The original audit is historical BEFORE evidence. Its assessments, logging gaps, tests, source hashes and prior device measurements are not post-remediation verification.
Ledger and worker-manifest statuses are reported claims with their original scope. Even a literal fixed status does not establish full integration or physical qualification.
Source implementation, reported host tests, final full-build/source identity, and actual physical target qualification are separate evidence layers.
A closeout can resolve integration for a specific canonical finding only. Global build or test results do not silently close individual findings.
Missing evidence stays unreported or pending. This generator does not run contributed checks, inspect their logs, certify the firmware, or infer a pass from an artifact path.
Host tests and source changes do not establish a real 30 FPS floor, optical quality, battery life, physical sensor accuracy, or long-term storage reliability.
App and module links retain the historical audit mapping. Shared-service and transitive app effects are not inferred. No mapped finding is not a clean bill of health.
Recorded source line numbers may have moved. Input JSON hashes identify this report's evidence snapshot, not a qualified firmware or ELF.

findings.evidence_scope: Reported changes and checks only. Consult original scope, per-ID closeout and global evidence; no physical qualification inferred.

evidence.detail: Picker immediately changes tz_min; prefs_save is called before exit.
Active loop applies changed preference to g_tz_offset_min and libc TZ.
Exit reads the already shifted local datetime, adds the old-to-new offset, then calls hal_set_datetime at1895. Preview1839 also adds the delta again.
mktime interprets the supplied wall time in the new timezone; settimeofday129 changes epoch and board_clock_changed130 queues RTC write.
Pending epoch is consumed by RTC save461; restore493 decodes UTC at next boot.
Simulator wall RTC is separate from sim_tz_min; it does not reproduce the firmware host preference application.

historical_before.impact: pick_commit changes the preference while the picker remains open. The host applies the new TZ before the exit; pick_leave then adds another 30 minutes and hal_set_datetime changes UTC by that amount. Larger selections can shift hours or dates; alarms, calendar/day grouping, journal epochs and filenames can become wrong. board_clock_changed queues this erroneous epoch for RTC persistence when the RTC write succeeds, so a reboot need not repair it. This is separate from world-clock display APP-013 and RTC write retry PLAT-010.
historical_before.recommendation: Keep UTC unchanged when selecting a display offset. Apply the offset once in the host; remove wall-clock mutation from picker exit and compute previews from a UTC anchor. Use calendar conversion instead of hand-written one-month rollover. Add firmware-like timezone/epoch invariance checks, including quarter-hour and date-boundary choices.
historical_before.title: Leaving the timezone picker changes UTC by the timezone delta again
historical_before.trigger: Open Settings > Time zone, change +05:30 to +06:00, let at least the next normal firmware loop run, then back out or receive a covering alert.
historical_before.verification: timezone_picker.log: actual picker exit with firmware-already-applied +06:00 wall11:00 sets11:30. Host/HAL/RTC chain inspected; physical RTC not exercised.

changes.detail: Compute selected-offset previews from UTC, independent of whether the host has applied the preference; unknown UTC is explicit.

evidence.detail: read_slot_status returns -1 for non-ENOENT fopen failure, read error, close failure or invalid contents, collapsing transient I/O uncertainty and confirmed invalidity.
newest_slot chooses the readable bank even if the other state is -1; only neither valid yields -2.
The load path accepts slot>=0 and marks ok true at 673, learning identities only for readable banks.
Recovered active/paused sessions immediately call checkpoint_request at 634.
write_checkpoint derives a/b from successful reads only; foreign guard at 538 inspects only valid readable banks.
With one readable bank, target=1-latest; fopen(path,"wb") at 562 truncates the unreadable other bank.

historical_before.impact: Recovery silently rolls back to the older session/history, reports ready/available with zero errors, then may destroy the only newer checkpoint. The foreign-card hash guard cannot identify a bank that could not be read. This is the workout recorder analogue of STOR-001; it is a separate call chain and file format.
historical_before.recommendation: Keep absent, validated-corrupt and unreadable states distinct. Defer authoritative recovery and all destructive bank writes while any existing bank has an unresolved I/O error; retry reads and retain an error/slot/errno. Preserve recovery lineage until both banks can be assessed.
historical_before.title: Unreadable latest workout bank can be overwritten by an older recovered checkpoint
historical_before.trigger: A previously valid latest workouts.N.bin returns a non-ENOENT read failure while the other, older bank is readable; that latest bank remains unreadable through the next checkpoint preflight but accepts a write. Recovery of the older active or paused session itself requests a checkpoint.
historical_before.verification: checks/health/workout_read_eio.json: actual workout.c and existing host test stubs, audit-only fopen EIO on latest bank reads until its first wb. Before: latest bank0 elapsed2000, bank1 elapsed1000. Reboot loads1000 ready1 available1 errors0; subsequent recovery save writes bank0 elapsed1000. Compile and assertion-backed observation pass; no device faults injected.

changes.detail: Separate valid, absent, confirmed corrupt and unresolved I/O. Authoritative recovery is deferred if either bank is unreadable; checked-write preflight refuses to truncate either bank until reads resolve. Retain operation, slot, errno and retryable unknown status.

changes.detail: Reviewed root's two persistent staging/published PSRAM buffers, mutex-serialized HTTP/BLE writers and reader counts. Newly allocated pointer publication now shares the reader lock (allocation stays outside it). Legacy raw accessor also acquires a pin instead of returning an already-released pointer; every accessor requires release.

evidence.detail: Server starts on station GOT_IP.
OTA routes are registered on that server.
Upload handler only checks the busy flag and creates the worker.
URL handler accepts a bounded URL body and starts the worker without the setup-session gate.
All three update routes register unconditionally.
Secure boot is not configured.
HTTP download is permitted by the OTA client configuration.

historical_before.impact: A valid application image can be installed without a watch-side update session or application-layer authorization. Image structural integrity and rollback are separate from authorizing an update. This source finding is preserved for the root reviewer; no update was attempted.
historical_before.recommendation: Require an explicit bounded update session initiated on the watch and an authorization check shared by every update entrypoint; qualify a signed-image policy if authenticated firmware is required.
historical_before.title: Firmware update routes lack the explicit setup-session gate
historical_before.trigger: The watch joins a station network and a client reaches its HTTP update routes.
historical_before.verification: Source and checked-in configuration review only. Root independently verifies reachability and intended deployment trust boundary.

changes.detail: Publish IMU/file, preference loading/dirty, workout and track admission policy on the UI thread under a short spinlock. HTTP tasks no longer read UI-owned workout/preferences directly. Default/unrefreshed policy fails closed; a claim needs a <=2-second-old snapshot. A later blocked snapshot aborts an active transfer.

Atomic single-writer claim binds to the original setup-session generation and a 180-second transfer deadline. Token validation is before body allocation/read/task launch. Ending/reopening Phone setup cannot revive a writer. ota_busy stays claimed through boot selection/reply/reboot.

Host mutation owner=2 competes atomically with OTA writer owner=1. A paired end publishes the resulting admission policy before releasing to owner=0, closing a check-busy-then-start race. Writer cleanup can only release its own owner=1; render/read-only work remains permitted.

Track successful esp_ota_begin ownership explicitly; abort only an owned open handle. esp_ota_end consumes its handle even on error. Recheck authorization after validation and before boot selection. Failed begin cannot abort an invalid handle.

Reject a successful begin with NULL handle; never perform/finish without a valid begin. Incremental perform checks generation/deadline, rejects incomplete data, handles expiry before finish as timeout, and calls exactly one finish or abort. Do not print private URLs.

HTTP raw URL bodies reject embedded NUL, control, whitespace and trailing garbage bytes. Public URL API has a bounded 512-byte absolute HTTP(S) URL contract; queued tasks revalidate their original writer lease.

SD keeps a mounted lease for the operation. Each bounded read opens/seeks/length-checks/reads/closes its descriptor under one short SD lock; no descriptor survives a lock timeout and no unbounded cleanup-lock retry remains. Check ferror/fclose and image capacity before opening a flash sink. SDK validation remains the final image check; rename failure retains update.bin.
Only log confirmation if esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback succeeds.

Actual complete ota.c exercises concurrent pthread CAS claims, all entrypoint authorization, stale/generation/dirty/loading/activity policy, HTTP memory/task/async/read/start/write/end faults, URL null/start/perform/incomplete/finish/expiry/deadline/NUL faults, and SD lease/lock/open/seek/read/close/size/write faults. Mock sinks assert single valid ownership and exact cleanup; reboot hook asserts the writer is still exclusive.

contributions.root_request: REQUIRED: call ota_poll() from the UI loop (also display-off loops). Wrap state-changing service/input/preference work with ota_activity_begin()/ota_activity_end() so the new policy is published before host ownership releases. A read of ota_busy() alone does not close admission races; use it for status and reject shutdown/restart while updating. Keep rendering/read-only work running. Updates intentionally fail closed until the poll hook is integrated.
target_validation: A real IDF compile/link, partition/bootloader rollback and actual SDK image/digest validation were not run. No flash/boot/NVS write occurred in these tests.

Session checks surround blocking SDK operations; an already executing SDK/socket call can overrun the 180-second limit by its own blocking duration (URL socket timeout configured 15 seconds). Final authorization is checked immediately before commit; do not promise cancellation of a commit already executing inside the SDK.

Reopening update.bin between 4096-byte SD reads bounds descriptor/lock cleanup but adds SD I/O. Length changes abort; final SDK validation rejects an inconsistent image. Qualify read/flash duration and stacks on target; future synchronous URL/SD callers must use internal-stack workers, never PSRAM/render stacks.
Root's host interlocks must be integrated before claiming end-to-end exclusion with recording/shutdown. The HTTP token/session policy is not an image-signing or secure-boot implementation.

Read-only engine freezes clock/bg/ticks/input/prefs, keeps cached draw path and defers IN_CANCEL until an owned normal scope. Side button/ota cancel can revoke session safely.
Strong firmware shutdown-pending admission flag plus weak portable fallback supplied for central root guards.

evidence.detail: read_slot collapses absence, corrupt payload, and I/O errors into false.
newest chooses any other readable checkpoint.
Target selection assumes failed read means safe overwrite.
wb truncates that slot before write/flush verification.

historical_before.impact: A failed save can turn an already durable latest setting into an older setting on reboot. The dirty RAM retry is retained, but cannot protect against a reset during the failure interval.
historical_before.recommendation: Return separate missing/corrupt/I/O statuses. Abort writes on ambiguous read failures. Publish a new checked generation through a staged file or otherwise preserve both existing valid generations until verification; retain SD lock/lease, fsync/readback and dirty retry.
historical_before.title: A transient checkpoint read error can destroy the newest previously durable preferences
historical_before.trigger: Newest-slot fopen/read fails transiently; save treats it as absent, selects the older slot as newest, opens the actual newest slot with wb, then that write fails.
historical_before.verification: Positive isolated regression includes actual prefs_disk.c and injects one read EIO plus one failed fwrite; expected current payload newest is replaced by older. checks/storage/prefs_read_error/result.log. The last device flash also observed the newest slot becoming unreadable and older racket preference returning; that observation alone does not prove this exact failure chain.

changes.detail: Typed missing/corrupt/I/O checkpoint reads; both banks classified before selection. Any ambiguous read aborts save without opening a write destination.
Newest intrinsic checked generation selected independently of requested schema size; mismatched newest payload reports CORRUPT rather than selecting an older compatible payload.
Alternate-bank save retains newest durable generation, checksum, fflush/fsync/readback and boolean failure contract for caller dirty retry.
Added prefs_disk_read_status and prefs_disk_load_status; retained boolean wrapper and mount lease/lock ownership contract.

contributions.fix: Unsupported intrinsic current/legacy payload versions keep portable preferences loading/dirty and block checkpoint writes. Newest valid bank remains selected independently of request size.
contributions.reproducer: An intrinsic checked 44-byte checkpoint with unsupported version 99 caused both bool schema probes to fail while HAL pending ended false. Defaults could be checkpointed over it.

contributions.fix: Grouped wrist/source/revision edit advances the durable revision and preserves the explicit side. Replaying an overlay after tombstone failure is idempotent.
contributions.reproducer: Explicit manual choice of the default wrist while authoritative card held the other side/revision 30 merged only source/revision, keeping the wrong wrist and regressing to revision 1.

contributions.fix: Nonblocking RAM-owner restore gate under SD mutex, paired-store admission, UI reload/complete-field merge, dirty known admission rejection, explicit unknown-state repair, and IMU cache invalidation. HAL owner now gates SD plus NVS mirrors in the same shared lock.
contributions.reproducer: Raw replacement of an authoritative SD bank was superseded by later clean/dirty stale RAM checkpoints. Cached IMU intent also remained loaded after raw replacement.

contributions.fix: Checked versioned/checksummed <=256-byte explicit whole-field mask overlay through separate NVS key; merge at fallback reboot and future card load. Never overwrite an unread/corrupt overlay. SD stays dirty/loading until verified; empty-mask tombstone must also verify before acknowledgement.
contributions.reproducer: Card-absent/unknown-SD explicit edits could not persist across reset without allowing a blind overwrite or altering the stale NVS mirror. HAL owner supplied the actual failing offline-create regression.

target_validation: Root HAL/prefs integration must retry unknown/corrupt SD boot state without NVS fallback or overwriting durable SD generations.
Real-card interrupted writes, mount removal/reinsert, fsync/readback under DMA pressure.

evidence.detail: SD host uses default allocation behavior; no reserved SD bounce-buffer owner is configured.
Failure hook captures final allocator failures.
Display DMA buffers are reserved at startup; SD/radio resource admission is not coordinated here.

historical_before.impact: Settings checkpointing, sensor history and diagnostic persistence failed together. The first flash was blocked safely; resetting recovered storage, but the runtime condition has no durable fix.
historical_before.recommendation: Give SD a guaranteed bounded DMA staging resource using the installed SDK host capability or a dedicated owner; include internal-DMA headroom in admission for radio/TLS/display/recording work. Measure the failing allocation window, then run an unplugged long-session soak with settings, diagnostics and recording concurrently.
historical_before.title: Historical prolonged runtime exhausted SD sector DMA allocation headroom
historical_before.trigger: On the previously running image, background operation eventually reached repeated 512-byte MALLOC_CAP_DMA allocation failures during SD I/O.
historical_before.verification: Observed on OLD pre-blur running firmware: build/continuous-trail-flash/{diagnose-checkpoint.log,recover.log,recovery-boot.log,flash.log}. SDK local esp_heap_caps.h identifies 0x8 as DMA; sdmmc_cmd.c allocate_dma_buf uses this capability. A later heap snapshot with free bytes does not disprove earlier transient allocation exhaustion. Root cause allocation owner/timing remains unresolved.

evidence.detail: Copies flash-package.ps1 into the distributed flash.ps1 and README directs users to it.

historical_before.impact: The package correctly uses separate segments and warns against flashing the merged image over NVS, but flash-package.ps1 immediately resets/writes through esptool. It never sends prefs flush or requires stored=1/match=1, so recent authoritative SD preferences can be lost across reboot. It also lacks the checked range validation used by flash_watch. NVS preservation alone does not establish SD preference durability.
historical_before.recommendation: Package a common checked flasher with segment manifest validation and explicit SD checkpoint acknowledgment. Preserve the existing merged-image warning; do not substitute another checkout. Keep C143 legacy variant flashing documented separately because it uses a different runtime.

evidence.detail: Animation time is stored as global float.
nos_dt is computed from elapsed_ms, then directly accumulated into nos_t at line2242 without an epoch/precision policy.
Authored frame count is derived from float nos_t minus float origin; tween progress uses the same difference at line327.
Touch long-press recognition compares the affected clock against P.t_down.
Existing clock test intentionally resets to a small origin at line58, so it does not cover uptime precision loss.
Current-engine test observed CLOCK origin=524288 requested=.025 actual=.000000000 while dt=.025000000.

historical_before.impact: Animations/deadlines drift well before the final freeze. At the freeze, frame count and nos_dt still advance but nos_t-based tweens, long press, toast/banner timeouts and power-sheet deadlines can stop completing. Wall uptime to encounter this depends on active/AOD/sleep frame cadence;524288 seconds is a clock value, not a claimed six-day wall-clock soak.
historical_before.recommendation: Represent monotonic animation deadlines with an integer64-bit clock and convert bounded relative intervals to float, or otherwise establish a consistent precision-preserving timestamp API. Merely changing the accumulator to double while leaving every app t0 as float does not solve relative-time precision.

historical_before.trigger: Accumulate a large active animation-clock origin. At nos_t=65536 seconds,25ms advances by23.4375ms; at131072 and262144 seconds it advances by31.25ms. At524288 seconds a25ms frame advances by0.

Overflow drops new queue events.

historical_before.impact: The 128-record diagnostic queue fills and drops new records; a 32-entry RTC ring retains only a recent suffix. Action/power history around a prolonged incident can disappear, just when it is needed most.
historical_before.recommendation: Prioritize fault/power/recording-transition events over routine events, reserve an emergency bounded channel independent of SD, record first/last/count summaries for repeated failures, and expose a sticky evidence-loss indication with an export bundle.
historical_before.title: Diagnostic evidence shares the failing SD resource and can overflow before recovery
historical_before.trigger: SD allocation/I/O failures stop the sports writer and the diagnostic consumer for minutes.
historical_before.verification: Observed pre-flash NOSLOG showed available0, queue128, >500 dropped and >4,000 storage errors. Current flash recovered this temporarily; longer-term retention behavior is not fixed.

changes.detail: Separate32-record priority capacity from128 routine slots in tracked PSRAM; drain faults/transitions first and keep separate routine/priority/emergency loss counters.

Independent8-slot checked RTC fault ledger pins immutable first evidence and updates last/count without overwriting first. Repeated faults coalesce; a torn mutable suffix preserves first, marks loss, and cold-power limits remain explicit.

Expose sticky evidence loss and retained fault summaries independently of SD through NOSEVIDENCE/NOSFAULT. Summaries/last occurrences replay when SD recovers; queue and fsync/readback behavior remains bounded.

findings.evidence_scope: Reported changes and checks only. Consult original scope, per-ID closeout and global evidence; no physical qualification inferred.

evidence.detail: One timestamp is captured before all seven sequential services.
ext_idle uses unsigned (now-last)>NOS_EXT_IDLE_MS.
GPS stops on that idle result; getter renews last_get at line 301.
LTE want_on uses the same helper; getters renew last_get at lines 407/420.
HR disables its user stream on this result; getter renews at line 306.

historical_before.impact: Unsigned now-last_get becomes nearly UINT32_MAX and passes the 8-second idle test. GPS, LTE, or HR can stop while a visible app or workout is renewing them; subsequent enables may restart them. A slow preceding service widens the timing window.
historical_before.recommendation: Use a wrap-safe signed elapsed comparison that treats a renewal newer than the captured time as fresh; synchronize lease state and refresh the service timestamp around potentially slow work.
historical_before.title: Concurrent getter renewal can immediately expire an external sensor lease
historical_before.trigger: The ext task captures now, then the UI renews last_get at a later millisecond before the task tests that lease.
historical_before.verification: Actual ext_idle/ext_due helper text was extracted unchanged and compiled. now=10000,last=10001 produced idle=1 although a renewed lease requires 0. Ordinary fresh, expired, and rollover controls behaved as expected; see checks/platform/lease_edge.json.

changes.detail: Preserved root signed wrap-safe elapsed helper. Future renewals are fresh rather than unsigned underflow.
Each slow module gets a newly sampled time. Sensor servicing excludes all audio file I/O; leases use guarded snapshots.
LTE refreshes service time after pumping UART and reads request ownership under ext_lock.

findings.evidence_scope: Reported changes and checks only. Consult original scope, per-ID closeout and global evidence; no physical qualification inferred.

evidence.detail: Background flag is set by the periodic scheduler.
A retained bg flag restarts a stopped device.
Pointer failures stop after ten errors but do not clear bg.
FIFO payload failure returns before timeout evaluation.
BG_MAX_MS and contact-loss checks are inside the successful nonempty FIFO branch.
Getter copies cache without age invalidation.
Workout accepts HR only with quality/range and sample_ms freshness gates.

historical_before.impact: The advertised 40-second background limit is checked only after a successful nonempty FIFO read. The LED stream can remain requested indefinitely; pointer failures call stop but leave bg set, causing another start. Old cached readings can also remain visible to callers that do not inspect sample_ms. Workout metrics explicitly check the 3-second freshness limit, reducing that consumer impact.
historical_before.recommendation: Apply the background deadline before any acquisition early return, cap restart attempts, clear acquisition state on persistent errors, and invalidate stale cached outputs consistently.
historical_before.title: Heart-rate background sampling has no effective timeout when FIFO acquisition fails
historical_before.trigger: A background MAX30102 measurement starts, then its FIFO remains empty, FIFO payload reads fail, or repeated pointer reads fail.
historical_before.verification: Reachable state-machine review; existing host suite does not inject MAX30102 FIFO or bus faults. Measure LED current and recovery on hardware with a controlled sensor fault.

changes.detail: Validated/preserved root 40-second background deadline before every empty/pointer/payload return, capped restart state and producer-time history/consumer owners.
Stale cached BPM/SpO2/quality invalidation retained; no getter refresh of acquisition time.
Added cumulative FIFO pointer/payload error and observed overflow-flag counters. Shutdown requires an acknowledged SHDN write; cancel retries an ambiguous transition before restarting.

evidence.detail: Shutdown only checks the IMU recorder and IMU browser.
Then calls board_prepare_sleep and esp_deep_sleep_start.
Preparation stops board/assets, unmounts SD and disables the onboard IMU; no external shutdown hook.
GPS backup requires an explicit UART command; no power gate wire.
LTE power-off is an asynchronous multi-step AT/key state machine.
HR shutdown is an explicit register write from the ext service.

historical_before.impact: The ESP enters deep sleep after stopping the board task and onboard IMU, but external device shutdown commands and file-close services have no completion barrier. VBAT-powered strap devices can continue consuming power after the UI says power off. Exact residual current depends on attached hardware and GPIO behavior and was not measured. Audio file ownership is also being reviewed independently by root.
historical_before.recommendation: Add an asynchronous platform shutdown coordinator: reject new work, stop each external stream, wait for owned files and hardware acknowledgments with bounded failure reporting, then unmount and sleep.
historical_before.title: Power-off does not coordinate shutdown of optional strap devices
historical_before.trigger: The user confirms POWER OFF while optional GPS, LTE, HR or audio streams are active.
historical_before.verification: Call-chain review and driver power model; validate shutdown under each attached module and measure final rail current.

changes.detail: Asynchronous idempotent begin/poll/cancel API: 0 pending, 1 only acknowledged clean, -1 error/timeout with continued progress. Cancel releases admission on ext task after any current hook returns.
Per-module acknowledged barriers and diagnostics; 30-second timeout reports error without fabricating hardware-off state. Cancellation cannot reuse an old hook ACK in a later cycle.
Reject new streams, wait real extf close/drain and exta I2S disable/delete/park ACK. Ambiguous fclose failure retains lease/error barrier; cancellation does not interrupt finalization.
AT shutdown, bounded key fallback and actual POWERED DOWN observation; cancel retains pending power-down in the normal FSM before a future enable can start.
Backup command must be fully TX-drained and UART deletion acknowledged. Cancel forces an explicit normal wake after an ambiguous prior command.
Haptic callback ownership plus PWM-zero ACK; HR/compass/light/environment require register ACKs and preserve failed-transition state for recovery.
Synthetic counterpart drains a real async file owner and WaveOut worker; recorder remains reusable after cancel and audio handles restart only after old worker cleanup.
Root-owned integration observed: host requires exactly clean external ACK plus board READY, retries failures and invokes cancel on abort. Not edited by this worker.

evidence.detail: FT3168 board_touch_read returns 0 for both failed I2C and no-contact data.
touch_poll treats the return directly as down.

historical_before.impact: s_touch_ok/s_imu_ok remain false; normal reads return absent without retry. Touch may be unusable for the whole boot, and walking/wrist wake/raw recording remain unavailable. Optional external hot-plug support is separately a missing feature, not assumed to be promised.
historical_before.recommendation: Use bounded backoff reprobe/reconfiguration for essential base devices, expose a retry control and first/last error, and avoid spinning/log flooding on genuine absence.

evidence.detail: Clock-change callback sets pending epoch and dirty.
Control-read and stop failures return silently.
Calendar/restart failure can mark RTC invalid, but caller receives no result.
Dirty is cleared before rtc_save and never restored on failure.

historical_before.impact: board_task clears s_rtc_dirty before invoking a void rtc_save. Failure is not requeued, so battery-backed RTC may retain old time or invalid state until another sync or explicit sleep attempt. Early control-read/stop failures return without the RTC warning or validity update.
historical_before.recommendation: Return write status, retain the pending request until success with bounded retry, use current trusted UTC when retrying, and log the failed register operation and retry/recovery event.
historical_before.title: RTC synchronization request is discarded before the write succeeds
historical_before.trigger: USB/BLE/NTP sets system time, then one RTC control read, stop command, calendar write, or restart fails.
historical_before.verification: Source-proven loss of retry state. Portable RTC encode/decode tests passed; I2C write-failure recovery is not covered.

changes.detail: Track request generation, trusted-source status and pending epoch; never clear pending before I2C success.

Return success only after control read, STOP, complete calendar write and restart ACK. Count failed operation/error and invalidate runtime RTC trust. If both calendar write and OS invalidation fail, leave oscillator stopped so reboot cannot trust mixed fields.
Retry at bounded5s intervals using current trusted UTC. Clear only the generation actually written; a newer clock notification remains pending. Shutdown forces a checked final attempt.
Initial RTC restore is serialized with retry and preserves retained system UTC after a failed RTC read. Later device reprobe never overwrites a subsequent radio/USB clock update.

historical_before.impact: The saved/tile state changes, but NimBLE still starts and remains connectable. The control therefore cannot deliver the battery or availability behavior implied by off. Current source intentionally keeps the phone link alive, which should be represented honestly in the UI.

evidence.detail: Loop captures now before earlier services and passes it to gps_service.

historical_before.recommendation: Refresh the monotonic timestamp after pump before stale checks, and use a wrap-safe elapsed helper that treats newer acquisition timestamps as fresh. Apply the same rule to lease and data timestamps across services.

evidence.detail: Legacy GET maps any fopen failure to MISSING.
Paced GET has the same mapping.
CRC query also maps any fopen failure to MISSING.
Host treats MISSING as a missing file, not a transient transport/storage failure.

historical_before.impact: SDGET/SDGET2/SDCRC return MISSING; host raises FileNotFoundError and deliberately avoids retry. Operators cannot tell absence from the failure mode that blocked the previous flash.
historical_before.recommendation: Reserve MISSING for ENOENT; return a typed operation/error/errno response for other failures. Keep retries bounded and read-only; include SD generation and resource telemetry in failure reports.
historical_before.title: Storage read failures are reported as missing files
historical_before.trigger: fopen fails because of low DMA memory, exhausted handles, permission errors, or I/O errors rather than a nonexistent path.
historical_before.verification: Source-backed reachable condition. Prior flash evidence checkpoint-read-2.log includes unreadable slot 0 while allocation failures were occurring; do not infer permanent file absence from that message.

changes.detail: Legacy GET returns MISSING only on ENOENT; all other open/read/seek/close failures return typed phase and errno. CRC pass checks fread errors.

CRC distinguishes actual absence and I/O. Dispatch emits command-specific unavailable/nomem/busy/path/recovery errors; directory read I/O is not reported as empty.
