evidence.detail: The recording filename is M_MMDD_HHMMSS.wav, without year or uniqueness test.
The start guard checks only microphone/path/active state, not an existing file.
fopen(path, wb) truncates an existing recording.
Month/day filename sorting also lacks year information.

findings.impact: The path contains no year, monotonic sequence, or collision suffix. The HAL opens it with wb, truncating the existing recording before any new samples are captured.
findings.recommendation: Allocate a unique persistent filename with full UTC date and a collision suffix or sequence; create it exclusively and retry on existence. Retain the full recording timestamp as metadata for chronological sorting and today labels.
findings.title: Recorder file naming can overwrite an existing recording
findings.trigger: Start a recording at a local month/day/hour/minute/second already used by an existing memo: for example after a manual clock rollback, timezone/DST clock repetition, next year, or two short starts in the same second after finalization.

verification.method: Direct application filename and actual HAL open mode inspection; no existing user files were touched.

evidence.detail: Picker immediately changes tz_min; prefs_save is called before exit.
Active loop applies changed preference to g_tz_offset_min and libc TZ.
Exit reads the already shifted local datetime, adds the old-to-new offset, then calls hal_set_datetime at1895. Preview1839 also adds the delta again.
mktime interprets the supplied wall time in the new timezone; settimeofday129 changes epoch and board_clock_changed130 queues RTC write.
Pending epoch is consumed by RTC save461; restore493 decodes UTC at next boot.
Simulator wall RTC is separate from sim_tz_min; it does not reproduce the firmware host preference application.

findings.impact: pick_commit changes the preference while the picker remains open. The host applies the new TZ before the exit; pick_leave then adds another 30 minutes and hal_set_datetime changes UTC by that amount. Larger selections can shift hours or dates; alarms, calendar/day grouping, journal epochs and filenames can become wrong. board_clock_changed queues this erroneous epoch for RTC persistence when the RTC write succeeds, so a reboot need not repair it. This is separate from world-clock display APP-013 and RTC write retry PLAT-010.
findings.recommendation: Keep UTC unchanged when selecting a display offset. Apply the offset once in the host; remove wall-clock mutation from picker exit and compute previews from a UTC anchor. Use calendar conversion instead of hand-written one-month rollover. Add firmware-like timezone/epoch invariance checks, including quarter-hour and date-boundary choices.
findings.title: Leaving the timezone picker changes UTC by the timezone delta again
findings.trigger: Open Settings > Time zone, change +05:30 to +06:00, let at least the next normal firmware loop run, then back out or receive a covering alert.
findings.verification: timezone_picker.log: actual picker exit with firmware-already-applied +06:00 wall11:00 sets11:30. Host/HAL/RTC chain inspected; physical RTC not exercised.

evidence.detail: read_slot_status returns -1 for non-ENOENT fopen failure, read error, close failure or invalid contents, collapsing transient I/O uncertainty and confirmed invalidity.
newest_slot chooses the readable bank even if the other state is -1; only neither valid yields -2.
The load path accepts slot>=0 and marks ok true at 673, learning identities only for readable banks.
Recovered active/paused sessions immediately call checkpoint_request at 634.
write_checkpoint derives a/b from successful reads only; foreign guard at 538 inspects only valid readable banks.
With one readable bank, target=1-latest; fopen(path,"wb") at 562 truncates the unreadable other bank.

findings.impact: Recovery silently rolls back to the older session/history, reports ready/available with zero errors, then may destroy the only newer checkpoint. The foreign-card hash guard cannot identify a bank that could not be read. This is the workout recorder analogue of STOR-001; it is a separate call chain and file format.
findings.recommendation: Keep absent, validated-corrupt and unreadable states distinct. Defer authoritative recovery and all destructive bank writes while any existing bank has an unresolved I/O error; retry reads and retain an error/slot/errno. Preserve recovery lineage until both banks can be assessed.
findings.title: Unreadable latest workout bank can be overwritten by an older recovered checkpoint
findings.trigger: A previously valid latest workouts.N.bin returns a non-ENOENT read failure while the other, older bank is readable; that latest bank remains unreadable through the next checkpoint preflight but accepts a write. Recovery of the older active or paused session itself requests a checkpoint.
findings.verification: checks/health/workout_read_eio.json: actual workout.c and existing host test stubs, audit-only fopen EIO on latest bank reads until its first wb. Before: latest bank0 elapsed2000, bank1 elapsed1000. Reboot loads1000 ready1 available1 errors0; subsequent recovery save writes bank0 elapsed1000. Compile and assertion-backed observation pass; no device faults injected.

evidence.detail: Fixed need = COVER_PX*COVER_PX*2; allocation uses exactly need.
Loop checks got < need, but recv at line 1385 requests total-got rather than remaining allocation capacity.
Cover handler is registered independently of setup_authorized.
Station GOT_IP starts the server.

findings.impact: The handler can write beyond its 125000-byte PSRAM allocation; memory corruption is a correctness risk independently of who sends the request. The station web server exposes the handler after association. No device or network request was made during this audit.
findings.recommendation: Reject content_len values other than the required image size before allocation or reception; bound each receive by remaining image capacity and publish only a complete staged image.
findings.title: HTTP cover reception can exceed its allocated image buffer
findings.trigger: A cover request declares a body larger than the fixed 250 x 250 RGB565 image.
findings.verification: Source-proven bound mismatch. Root owns independent defensive review; no reproduction tooling or traffic was used.

evidence.detail: Server starts on station GOT_IP.
OTA routes are registered on that server.
Upload handler only checks the busy flag and creates the worker.
URL handler accepts a bounded URL body and starts the worker without the setup-session gate.
All three update routes register unconditionally.
Secure boot is not configured.
HTTP download is permitted by the OTA client configuration.

findings.impact: A valid application image can be installed without a watch-side update session or application-layer authorization. Image structural integrity and rollback are separate from authorizing an update. This source finding is preserved for the root reviewer; no update was attempted.
findings.recommendation: Require an explicit bounded update session initiated on the watch and an authorization check shared by every update entrypoint; qualify a signed-image policy if authenticated firmware is required.
findings.title: Firmware update routes lack the explicit setup-session gate
findings.trigger: The watch joins a station network and a client reaches its HTTP update routes.
findings.verification: Source and checked-in configuration review only. Root independently verifies reachability and intended deployment trust boundary.

evidence.detail: read_slot collapses absence, corrupt payload, and I/O errors into false.
newest chooses any other readable checkpoint.
Target selection assumes failed read means safe overwrite.
wb truncates that slot before write/flush verification.

findings.impact: A failed save can turn an already durable latest setting into an older setting on reboot. The dirty RAM retry is retained, but cannot protect against a reset during the failure interval.
findings.recommendation: Return separate missing/corrupt/I/O statuses. Abort writes on ambiguous read failures. Publish a new checked generation through a staged file or otherwise preserve both existing valid generations until verification; retain SD lock/lease, fsync/readback and dirty retry.
findings.title: A transient checkpoint read error can destroy the newest previously durable preferences
findings.trigger: Newest-slot fopen/read fails transiently; save treats it as absent, selects the older slot as newest, opens the actual newest slot with wb, then that write fails.
findings.verification: Positive isolated regression includes actual prefs_disk.c and injects one read EIO plus one failed fwrite; expected current payload newest is replaced by older. checks/storage/prefs_read_error/result.log. The last device flash also observed the newest slot becoming unreadable and older racket preference returning; that observation alone does not prove this exact failure chain.

evidence.detail: Creation fallback is unconditional after update-open failure.
Successful new write advances queue and reports success despite loss of the older file.

findings.impact: All prior records in that hourly/daily file are lost and status.available is reported true. Historical low-DMA errors motivate testing this path; they do not prove this exact truncate sequence occurred on the watch.
findings.recommendation: Create only on a confirmed ENOENT; preserve and retry on EIO/ENOMEM/EMFILE. Retain update-mode append at the validated tail and explicit torn-tail recovery; a plain a+b substitution would defeat seek-based recovery. Log operation, errno, path ID and retained queue count.
findings.title: Journal append fallback can truncate existing sports and sensor history
findings.trigger: fopen(existing_path,"r+b") fails with a transient error other than ENOENT; a subsequent fopen(path,"w+b") succeeds.
findings.verification: Positive regression executes the extracted current drain body with a transient r+b EIO and verifies the existing record disappears while status.available stays true. checks/storage/journal_open_error/result.log.

evidence.detail: intent_load skips every failed fopen without distinguishing ENOENT from I/O failure.
Loaded is set even when no slot could be read.
Worker retries load only while not intent_loaded.
No loaded active/dirty state means no pending resume.

findings.impact: The loader permanently marks intent loaded, sets inactive/uncorrupted, and reports no pending work. The crash-resume guarantee is lost without a visible checkpoint error for that boot; an explicit user start or later healthy reboot can recover.
findings.recommendation: Keep the resume state unknown and retry with backoff after read/I/O errors; only settle inactive after confirmed absence or the newest proven inactive generation, with no unreadable slot that might be newer. Expose loading/unknown/corrupt/active states and log which slot/operation failed.
findings.title: Recording auto-resume is silently suppressed by temporary checkpoint read failures
findings.trigger: At boot, both intent checkpoint fopen calls fail transiently while a valid active intent remains on the card.
findings.verification: Positive regression executes the actual intent_load body with two read EIOs; active checked record remains on disk but imu_worker_pending returns false. checks/storage/imu_intent_read_error/result.log.

evidence.detail: do_put stages in a .part file.
Original is removed before publication succeeds.
Failed rename deletes .part too.

findings.impact: Both original and new data are deleted; an error response does not restore the original. This can affect recordings, preferences, textures, or any user path accepted by the transfer protocol.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit backup/publication protocol supported by FATFS: preserve original until new file is durable and rename succeeds, recover interrupted transactions at mount, and require an opt-in replacement mode for critical settings/active recordings.
findings.title: Failed upload publication can delete the original file
findings.trigger: An upload replaces an existing path, closes its .part file, removes the original, then rename fails.
findings.verification: Positive isolated regression executes the current do_put body with a rename EIO and verifies neither original nor staged file survives. No real device file was touched. checks/storage/upload_rename_error/result.log.

evidence.detail: SD host uses default allocation behavior; no reserved SD bounce-buffer owner is configured.
Failure hook captures final allocator failures.
Display DMA buffers are reserved at startup; SD/radio resource admission is not coordinated here.

findings.impact: Settings checkpointing, sensor history and diagnostic persistence failed together. The first flash was blocked safely; resetting recovered storage, but the runtime condition has no durable fix.
findings.recommendation: Give SD a guaranteed bounded DMA staging resource using the installed SDK host capability or a dedicated owner; include internal-DMA headroom in admission for radio/TLS/display/recording work. Measure the failing allocation window, then run an unplugged long-session soak with settings, diagnostics and recording concurrently.
findings.title: Historical prolonged runtime exhausted SD sector DMA allocation headroom
findings.trigger: On the previously running image, background operation eventually reached repeated 512-byte MALLOC_CAP_DMA allocation failures during SD I/O.
findings.verification: Observed on OLD pre-blur running firmware: build/continuous-trail-flash/{diagnose-checkpoint.log,recover.log,recovery-boot.log,flash.log}. SDK local esp_heap_caps.h identifies 0x8 as DMA; sdmmc_cmd.c allocate_dma_buf uses this capability. A later heap snapshot with free bytes does not disprove earlier transient allocation exhaustion. Root cause allocation owner/timing remains unresolved.

evidence.detail: Only GPS valid and allocated point storage are required; no recovery state is maintained.
Distance is always measured from the last accepted point.
d > 500 returns before updating the anchor; repeating normal fixes cannot recover.
The HAL correctly invalidates stale fixes, so a normal outage can reach the service recovery path.

findings.impact: Recording remains active, but every subsequent position is rejected and both saved route and accumulated distance omit the remaining journey until the user returns within 500 m of the old point.
findings.recommendation: Track the last observation and fix-gap age separately from the last stored point. On a plausible reacquisition after a gap, begin a new GPX segment/reanchor without counting the unobserved gap; preserve a bounded speed/quality outlier filter.
findings.title: A GPS gap over 500 metres permanently freezes the track anchor
findings.trigger: Record two points, lose GPS while moving over 500 m from the last accepted point, then reacquire and continue away from it.

verification.result: Actual svc_track.c: after 200 later valid fixes, point count stayed 2, distance stayed 11.12 m, active stayed 1.

evidence.detail: show_now becomes false after STALE_S when no current fix exists.
The action becomes A_NONE before considering svc_track_active().
No NOW page/action is drawn when show_now is false.
The stop hit target is explicitly gated by show_now.
The sole production call to svc_track_stop is this screen's stop_track().

findings.impact: The track and GPS continue running, but the NOW page shows the sky without Stop. The user must regain GPS to stop/save through the UI; no other production caller of svc_track_stop exists.
findings.recommendation: Make recording state determine Stop availability independently of fix state. Keep a Stop/save action on the searching and module-absent pages and on reopening an active session.
findings.title: Navigate removes the only Stop control after prolonged GPS loss
findings.trigger: Start recording and lose the fix for at least 30 seconds, or reopen an active recording before a fresh fix arrives.

verification.result: Actual nav_tick(): active=1, after loss action=A_NONE, on_rec_button=0.

evidence.detail: N.stale means only a short post-loss window, rather than all times that the retained fix is stale.
Dimming targets 0 once that short window ends.
Home distance and bearing use retained N.last whenever have_last is set.
TRACK colors its current-location marker from the dim value.
BACK may announce arrival from home_dist derived from the retained fix.
The no-fix fallback is bypassed whenever any last fix exists.

findings.impact: The old location, arrow, and start distance continue to be used but their stale dimming fades back to the live appearance. BACK TO START can continue saying YOU ARE AT THE START based on the old fix without a current-fix warning.
findings.recommendation: Separate fix validity/age from the NOW-page retention timeout. Keep stale styling and a clear age/no-fix state on every navigation page, and gate arrival confirmation on a current qualified fix.
findings.title: Old BACK/TRACK guidance regains live brightness after 30 seconds without GPS
findings.trigger: While a retained track and last fix exist, remain without a new fix beyond the 30-second NOW-page stale interval, then view BACK TO START or TRACK.

verification.result: Actual nav_tick(): dim=1 during short loss, then dim=0 and stale=0 while have_last=1 and GPS remains invalid.

evidence.detail: Stopping changes T.active=0 before write_gpx() returns a result.
A second stop returns -1 when inactive, preventing a save retry.
Starting resets both point count and distance.
All save failures are reduced to saved_state=2, including write errors unrelated to card absence.
The summary expires into Start rather than Retry save.

findings.impact: svc_track_stop turns active off before the write and later calls return -1. Navigate shows a short NO SD CARD summary and then offers Start, whose implementation discards the retained points. No pending-save/retry UI or durable session recovery exists.
findings.recommendation: Retain an explicit unsaved session after stop and allow retry/export until successful or explicitly discarded. Save via a worker with mount lease, shared lock, checked flush/fsync/close, and atomic publication; root's storage audit owns the common SD lifecycle findings.
findings.title: A failed track save cannot be retried before starting discards the session
findings.trigger: Stop a track with at least two points while the SD card is absent or a file write/open fails; restore the card and try to save that track.

verification.method: Cross-checked full production callers and all return paths; no card/device fault injection performed.
verification.related_scope: Shared SD transaction/lease findings are owned by the root storage review.

evidence.detail: Every device load rebuilds the memo list from the card.
readdir stops when n reaches MEMO_MAX, rather than considering later entries.
Sorting happens only after that truncated enumeration.
Completing a device recording reloads through the same truncated scanner.

findings.impact: Enumeration stops at 24 before sorting. With the usual creation/name order, newer recordings are absent from the app even after reopening, while save confirmation still succeeds. A directory with 25 fixture memos reproduced omission of the newest file.
findings.recommendation: Scan the full directory and retain the newest 24 using a bounded selection structure, or provide pagination. Show the total/count limit and an export/delete route so saved files remain discoverable.
findings.title: Recorder scans only the first 24 files before choosing displayed memos
findings.trigger: Keep more than 24 WAV files in /watch/memos, as happens after repeated successful recordings.

verification.result: Device-side scanner compiled on the host with only MEMO_DIR redirected: 25 files, 24 displayed, newest_file_in_list=0.

evidence.detail: hal_rec_stop sets rec_stop_req and returns without finalization.
hal_rec_active becomes false as soon as the request is set.
Write error sets rec_err in the asynchronous service.
Header rewrite and fclose occur later in audio_service.
svc_memo_stop immediately runs rec_finish, success feedback, and saved toast.
A self-stop from card-full/error also uses rec_stop's success path.

findings.impact: hal_rec_stop only requests an asynchronous stop, but the app clears s_rec_open, reloads/stats the still-open file, and immediately announces SAVED/success. Final buffered samples, WAV length header, and fclose may not be complete; real disk errors follow the same success path. Displayed duration can be derived from an incomplete file.
findings.recommendation: Expose recorder states RECORDING, FINALIZING, SAVED, and ERROR with a completion result and written/dropped sample counts. Add the file to the list and confirm only after checked finalization; surface recoverable/truncated recordings accurately.
findings.title: Recorder confirms SAVED before finalization and cannot distinguish disk failure
findings.trigger: Stop a memo manually, or let the recorder stop itself because the card fills or an I/O error occurs.

verification.result: Actual app stop plus extracted actual HAL stop/active functions: toast=SAVED 0:01 while audio_recording=1 and stop_request=1.

evidence.detail: Pushing another screen invokes the covered screen's leave callback.
Compass leave calls hal_mag_calibrate(0) whenever M_CAL is displayed, even on cover.
Reveal enter returns without restarting or reconciling calibration.
Finish sets calibrating=0, and insufficient coverage keeps the previous calibration.
Stopped calibration reports 0 for an uncalibrated device or 1 for an old valid calibration.

findings.impact: leave always finishes/stops HAL calibration, but reveal enter returns early and keeps M_CAL. With no previous valid calibration, progress stays at zero and the figure-eight UI cannot complete. With an old calibration, the preserved UI may instead accept the old completed status as the new attempt's result.
findings.recommendation: Preserve an in-progress calibration on a cover, or deliberately cancel it and move to a resumable prompt. Reconcile HAL calibration state on reveal and distinguish cancelled/failed/successful completion.
findings.title: A covering screen stops compass calibration without resuming it
findings.trigger: Briefly cover the Compass during an unfinished calibration with a call, timer/alarm, or Find Watch alert, then reveal it while magnetometer samples remain available.

verification.result: Actual Compass leave/reveal: mode=M_CAL, calibrating=0.

evidence.detail: tick_level initializes acceleration to a synthetic flat vector.
The failed-read path retains that vector and has no unavailable flag.
The resulting center bubble qualifies as level_ok.
Level can be opened based on Compass mode alone, without an IMU capability/read guard.

findings.impact: A failed hal_imu_read leaves the default acceleration (0,0,1), producing a centered bubble, zero tilt, and FLAT despite no measurement. The optional-sensor contract is not reflected in this internal screen.
findings.recommendation: Track IMU validity and render a sensor unavailable/stale state. Only show tilt or FLAT after a qualified sample; retain the magnetometer's separate availability state.
findings.title: Compass Level claims FLAT when the IMU is unavailable
findings.trigger: Use a present/calibrated magnetometer but fail/remove the base IMU, then long-press into Level.

verification.method: Examined the actual failed-read branch and Level input/draw lifecycle. Hardware removal/failure was not exercised.

evidence.detail: hal_lte_sms_send explicitly returns 1 for queued.
Queue acceptance becomes R.result=1 immediately.
The successful reader auto-pops after 1.3 s.
R.result>0 is rendered as SENT.
Prompt/body failures increment sent_fail asynchronously.
Queueing returns success before the AT send completes.

findings.impact: The reader immediately shows SENT and success feedback, then closes after 1.3 s. Actual modem completion can take up to 60 s and may fail; there is no app completion/error path for that request.
findings.recommendation: Return a send request ID and expose queued/sending/sent/failed status. Keep the result pending until modem acceptance, and permit retry on the actual failure without falsely confirming delivery.
findings.title: Cellular reports SENT when an SMS was merely queued
findings.trigger: Tap any supported quick reply while the modem accepts the send request, then let registration, SIM, prompt, or network sending fail.

verification.result: Actual reply_send() with the documented queued return sets result=1 and FB_SUCCESS before completion.

evidence.detail: Opening a message clears app cache and invokes hal_lte_sms_mark_read.
The HAL mark-read implementation only edits L->sms[i].unread and the count.
Every new scan trusts the modem's REC UNREAD flag.
Inbox refreshes occur every 60 s and on dirty notification.
CMGL with mode 1 lists without marking read; there is no production CMGR operation in this driver.

findings.impact: The app and HAL clear unread only in RAM. The mode-1 CMGL command deliberately preserves SIM read state, and no CMGR or other read-state operation is sent, so the next refresh restores REC UNREAD and its badge.
findings.recommendation: Keep the SIM's stable message index and issue the supported modem read-state update, or persist a local read overlay keyed to a stable message identity. Reconcile that overlay on every refresh.
findings.title: Read SMS messages become unread again on the next inbox poll
findings.trigger: Open an unread SMS, return to Cellular status so its getter keeps LTE active, and let the next periodic or incoming-message-triggered CMGL refresh complete; then reopen the inbox.

verification.method: Traced reader -> HAL mark-read -> CMGL publication and searched all modem commands; no physical modem test.

evidence.detail: The app takes its SMS snapshot on inbox_enter.
Inbox tick does not refresh or bind rows to a stable message identifier.
Reader marks the message by s_open, a row index.
Background publish sorts newest-first and replaces the driver list.
Mark-read uses the same integer as the current driver's index.

findings.impact: The app's displayed message remains from the old s_sms array, but mark_read(s_open) applies the old row index to the new driver order. The wrong message and unread count are changed.
findings.recommendation: Include stable modem message IDs and snapshot generation in hal_sms. Resolve read/update operations by ID rather than by a transient row position, and refresh inbox counts as its generation changes.
findings.title: An inbox refresh can make opening one SMS mark another SMS read
findings.trigger: Leave the app inbox open and receive a newer SMS while the modem is still active (for example within the eight-second lease after inbox entry), so an incoming-triggered driver scan replaces/reorders its cached list; then open a row from the app's older snapshot.

verification.method: Application snapshot and driver mutation ordering checked; the UI task and driver task can reach the sequence without unsynchronized array access.

evidence.detail: local_offset_min compares only local and UTC time-of-day and discards calendar day.
The accepted range spans 26 hours and cannot uniquely unwrap that difference.
The inferred offset determines city day rollover and relative offset.
Weekday is based on that erroneous rollover.

findings.impact: Time-of-day subtraction infers UTC-11 instead of UTC+13. London displays the correct clock hour modulo 24 but the wrong weekday/day relationship and a relative offset differing by 24 h. Similar ambiguity exists for overlapping positive/negative offset ranges.
findings.recommendation: Use the authoritative configured/effective timezone offset or calculate local-civil-epoch minus UTC using the full date. Add tests around UTC-12, UTC+12/+13/+14 and date-line rollover.
findings.title: World Clock infers the wrong day and relative offset in overlapping extreme timezones
findings.trigger: Use a valid UTC epoch and a configured positive extreme timezone, e.g. UTC+13 at 2026-10-21 16:00 UTC (local Thursday 05:00), and view London.

verification.result: Configured +780 min inferred -660; London Thursday/same day/+720 instead of Wednesday/previous day/-720.

evidence.detail: Changing location explicitly invalidates the HAL cache.
The HAL exposes stale after one hour.
An invalid HAL cache leaves the existing NOS weather unchanged.
A valid HAL cache is copied without stale/age metadata.
The phone freshness window only selects a source; it does not expire old NOS data when HAL has none.
Any w->valid is immediately WS_OK irrespective of observation time or connection state.

findings.impact: NOS ignores HAL stale/age metadata. If HAL later invalidates its cache on a city change, wx_from_hal simply returns and preserves the prior valid feed. App/widget treat any valid bit as WS_OK and show old weather with no age/source warning.
findings.recommendation: Propagate source, observed age, fetching/error status, and location generation through svc_weather_t. Invalidate on explicit location change, keep stale content visibly dated, and never label old-city data as a successful new-city feed.
findings.title: Weather retains invalidated and indefinitely stale data as current
findings.trigger: Receive weather, then stay offline long enough for it to become stale, or change the configured weather city while the next fetch cannot complete.

verification.result: HAL valid=0/New city leaves NOS valid=1/Old city; a two-day stale HAL snapshot was accepted without qualification.

evidence.detail: weather_hour and weather_day carry epoch; hal_weather also carries utc_offset_seconds.
wx_merge_forecast copies only values/conditions and discards per-entry timestamps.
Display hour/weekday always come from the current watch local datetime.
Hourly labels are generated from current hour + 1 + row, regardless of forecast epoch.
Daily row zero is always TODAY, and later labels use current watch weekday.

findings.impact: HAL forecast entries carry UTC timestamps and the location's UTC offset, but the service drops them. The app labels unchanged cached values using current watch hour+1 and weekday+i; an old/yesterday or other-location entry is presented as a new future hour/TODAY.
findings.recommendation: Preserve entry epochs and the forecast location timezone. Select entries against the current trusted epoch, render their actual local times/dates, and drop expired entries rather than moving their labels.
findings.title: Weather forecast values are relabelled with the watch's current hours and days
findings.trigger: Keep a forecast through an hour/day boundary, or use a configured weather location with a different timezone from the watch.

verification.method: Traced actual HAL schema, service conversion, and app label creation; no live HTTP request was needed.

evidence.detail: The ended-screen branch begins cleanup tracking.
If it is covered and no transition runs, pushed/ending are cleared without removing the stack entry.
Alarm ring enter builds a default ALARM even when svc_alarm_ringing() is -1.
Its tick has no service-state ended guard.
Timer ring tick likewise does not dismiss when the service timer is inactive.
Find Watch initializes was_active from the already-ended state, preventing its false-after-true auto-close check on reveal.

findings.impact: ring_screen clears pushed merely because the alert is not on top. It does not remove the covered stack entry. Later it no longer owns cleanup; alarm/timer reveal initialization does not reject their ended service state, so a stale alert remains visible/awake and may require explicit user dismissal. Find Watch has a similar was_active-on-reveal limitation.
findings.recommendation: Retain alert ownership while covered and reconcile/remove ended entries on reveal, or give every ring screen a service generation plus an ended-state close path. Verify simultaneous and nested alarms, timers, calls, and Find Watch transitions.
findings.title: An ended alert covered by another alert can remain orphaned in the screen stack
findings.trigger: Let an alarm or timer alert expire/end while another ring screen covers it; then dismiss the covering ring.

verification.result: Actual ring_screen() with a narrow stack seam: want=0, pushed=0, but ALARM remains the top entry after the cover is popped.

evidence.detail: Music requests gestures only on enter.
Control handlers require engine IN_AIR events.
The request auto-expires after NOS_EXT_IDLE_MS without refresh.
Queue drain is also the gesture keepalive.
nos_air is the event injection entry, but whole-repo production call-site search found no hardware caller.
The diagnostic drains gesture data locally without forwarding it to Music.

findings.impact: Music enables the gesture engine once and handles IN_AIR, but production code never drains hal_light_gesture into nos_air. The only hardware drain is the Modules diagnostic. The gesture driver also disables the engine after eight idle seconds because Music never refreshes/drains it. Simulator air injection can conceal the missing device path.
findings.recommendation: Have one active-consumer-aware hardware input pump drain APDS gestures into nos_air, refreshing demand only where gestures are used. Release demand on leave and test the production HAL path beyond eight seconds.
findings.title: Music air gestures are not delivered from hardware and stop being requested
findings.trigger: Open Music on a watch with the APDS gesture sensor and attempt the implemented up/down/left/right controls.

verification.method: Whole-repo call-site search and driver idle/service lifecycle inspection. Physical gesture recognition remains an unverified hardware capability.

evidence.detail: The editor binds to s_edit_idx only.
ed_valid checks index bounds, not table generation or alarm identity.
The wheels are initialized from the selected alarm only when entering.
Each tick copies the retained wheel time into whichever alarm now occupies that index.
Gadgetbridge synchronization clears and replaces the entire alarm table in the service tick.
Leaving saves the editor's mutations.

findings.impact: The editor retains only the numeric index and its old drum values. If the new table still has that index, ed_valid passes; the next edit tick writes the old wheel time into the replacement alarm and leaving persists it. No generation/identity check detects the replacement.
findings.recommendation: Give alarm tables a generation and alarms stable identities. On remote replacement, rebind/reload the editor or close it with a visible update message; never apply a stale draft to a new alarm solely because its row number matches.
findings.title: Phone alarm synchronization can silently overwrite a different alarm being edited
findings.trigger: Open an existing watch alarm editor, then receive a Gadgetbridge alarm-list replacement containing a different alarm at that same index while the editor remains open.

verification.method: Traced phone_tick before app tick, full-table replacement, editor validity, drum update, and leave persistence. No paired phone used.

evidence.detail: Inbox entry refreshes the SMS list and renews the radio lease only once.
Inbox tick only advances UI/pending navigation and never refreshes LTE demand.
Reader tick also has no LTE demand/getter keepalive.
enabled is cleared after last_get expires when no send is pending.
The service requests modem power-off when demand expires.
NOS_EXT_IDLE_MS is eight seconds.

findings.impact: The driver's request expires and it powers the modem off even though the user is actively using a Cellular screen. New messages/registration updates stop until returning to the status screen or another action wakes the modem; app inbox contents and enabled preference do not reveal that power transition.
findings.recommendation: Keep an explicit LTE lease while any foreground Cellular status/inbox/reader screen requires live connectivity, and release it on leave. Show actual radio state if cached-only/offline browsing is intentional.
findings.title: The LTE radio loses its lease while the SMS inbox or reader is still open
findings.trigger: Enter the SMS inbox or reader with radio enabled and remain there for more than NOS_EXT_IDLE_MS (8 s), without queuing a reply or another LTE getter being called.

verification.method: Traced all LTE getter/list call sites, screen-stack ticking semantics and driver want_on/power-off guards. A pending send is an inspected exception and renews demand.

evidence.detail: I_GPS points to gps_auto.
Generic toggle writes preference, animation and prefs_save only.
Control Center changes same preference and calls hal_gps_enable(on).
Only additional gps_auto reader342 is under #ifndef ESP_PLATFORM.
Driver enable and getter lease state are independent from nos_prefs.

findings.impact: The Settings row and Control Center display the same bit, but only the tile calls hal_gps_enable. No active ESP firmware consumer applies gps_auto on boot or preference change; its other reader is inside the simulator-only Sports path. The row cannot reliably start/stop the configured GPS demand and the persisted display can disagree with the radio demand. This does not imply GPS getters stop requesting their own leases.
findings.recommendation: Define auto versus explicit GPS demand and apply the preference through one shared routine from both controls and boot. Expose actual demand, lease owner and powered state separately in Modules.
findings.title: Settings GPS auto changes a preference with no device-side consumer
findings.trigger: Toggle Settings > GPS auto on an equipped watch and compare with the Control Center GPS tile, or reboot after saving the setting.
findings.verification: Repository-wide gps_auto caller search, active compile manifest and driver enable/get paths inspected; no physical receiver test.

evidence.detail: flip(I_WRIST) changes only nos_prefs.wrist_left and saves.
Learn reading angle directly invokes wake_service_learn.
Configuration selects view by s_cfg.wrist; default is0 at55.
Independent wrist changes only through this setter.
Learning writes next.view[next.wrist].
NOS initializes wake from raise_wake only.
The legacy Settings UI does call the setter, but it is inactive for current1.43-B NOS.

findings.impact: Settings changes nos_prefs.wrist_left, while wake_service chooses and learns s_cfg.view[s_cfg.wrist]. That independent stored wrist defaults left and current NOS never calls wake_service_set("wrist",...). A right-wrist selection therefore does not select the right wake pose; learning overwrites the currently selected wake_cfg hand. A legacy UI has the setter but is not in the active NOS build.
findings.recommendation: Unify the wrist authority or explicitly migrate/synchronize the wake wrist when Settings changes. Translate left/right enum meanings carefully. Preserve the two learned poses and expose which one is active in the learning result.
findings.title: Wrist selection and learned wake position use independent wrist values
findings.trigger: Select the right wrist in current Settings, then use Learn reading angle or expect an existing per-wrist reading pose to switch.
findings.verification: All wake_service_set callers and NOS serial wake handler inspected. Incorrect hand selection is proven; physical gesture sensitivity impact is unmeasured.

evidence.detail: Leave always zeroes password and show flag, without nos_leaving_covered guard.
Keyboard screen uses that leave handler and no enter callback.
Screen cover calls leave through the engine lifecycle; nos_push uses call_cover at285.

findings.impact: nos_push invokes the covered screen leave callback. keyboard_leave unconditionally clears N.pass, and the keyboard has no enter callback to restore a draft. The same password field is revealed empty and connection attempts can fail after an unrelated interruption.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the in-memory draft on a temporary cover; scrub it when the user actually leaves, connects or cancels. Add a cover/reveal test with no secret text in logs.
findings.title: Covering the Wi-Fi keyboard erases an unfinished password
findings.trigger: Type part of a Wi-Fi password, then receive an alarm/call screen that covers the keyboard; dismiss it.
findings.verification: wifi_keyboard_cover.log includes actual callback: a12-byte draft becomes0 while the password field remains selected.

evidence.detail: mod_present returns1 for board modules including Motion.
sample retains the separate hal_imu_read return in V.imu_ok.
Motion detail formats gravity, tilt and vectors without validity guard.
Detail absent-state gate uses mod_present, not V.imu_ok.

findings.impact: The Modules list correctly reports no reply through V.imu_ok, but Motion detail treats all non-extension board modules as present and formats V.imu without checking imu_ok. It can show zero tilt or retained vectors and an apparently live level for unavailable data.
findings.recommendation: Gate the Motion detail and bubble on the same freshness/validity decision as the list; show unavailable or last-good age and retain an explicit retry state.
findings.title: Modules Motion detail displays numbers even after the IMU read fails
findings.trigger: Open Modules > Motion while the board IMU getter returns failure, including a subsequent I2C outage.
findings.verification: List/detail/read-return paths inspected. This is an app validity defect, not proof of the user-reported Battery/Health crash.

evidence.detail: Light check polls the cached getter and accumulates values.
lt_n counts getter polls, not unique acquisitions.
At10+ identical lux/proximity polls it fails READING FROZEN.
Compass has a related no-change predicate; hardware motion is not inferred here.

findings.impact: Each UI poll is counted as a read and equality of extrema is treated as proof of a stopped stream. A steady functioning sensor fails READING FROZEN. No sample sequence or age establishes acquisition liveness; the UI does not request a stimulus before that automatic verdict. Similar equality-based mic/mag checks warrant explicit stimulus semantics.
findings.recommendation: Use sample timestamps or acquisition sequence numbers for liveness. If response-to-motion/light is tested, prompt for a controlled change and distinguish inconclusive from failed.
findings.title: Diagnostics mistakes legitimate constant light readings for a frozen sensor
findings.trigger: Run Diagnostics with a working light sensor held in darkness and stable proximity, producing fresh valid0-lux/0-proximity readings for4 seconds.
findings.verification: diag_constant_light.log:160 deliberately fresh valid constant samples were classified ST_FAIL/READING FROZEN by the actual test routine.

evidence.detail: Old data is freed before malloc; failure215 returns withNULL and old size.
Load checks size only, then memcpy234 from the possiblyNULL value.
Interactive persistence truncates the single mirror directly, unlike firmware paired checksummed checkpoints.

findings.impact: hal_store_save_checked returns failure after destroying the prior RAM value; size remains the prior positive value and hal_store_load can memcpy from NULL. Simulator failure behavior violates the checked-store contract and cannot validate that a failed preference save preserves the last good state. Interactive file persistence also uses direct wb replacement rather than the real SD checkpoints.
findings.recommendation: Allocate a replacement first, commit only after success, and leave old state intact on failure. Provide a firmware-compatible checkpoint fixture or clearly separate generic simulator storage from durability tests.
findings.title: Simulator store replacement frees the old value before a fallible allocation
findings.trigger: Save an existing simulated key, then force allocation failure on replacement and subsequently load the same-sized key.
findings.verification: sim_store_allocation.log:old42 saved, forced allocation failure leaves slotdataNULL,size4. The crash-causing NULL copy was inferred, not executed.

evidence.detail: Compile failures throw only for -Strict or missing old object.
Default explicitly warns then links last-good objects.
All named outputs share build/nos_obj or nos_obj_nocost.
Documentation explains fallback; therefore this is not described as a hidden behavior.

findings.impact: The build deliberately links the last good object, prints a warning, and can exit successfully. The resulting executable mixes source revisions but has no per-object provenance/degraded marker for downstream test/capture tools. A named -Out binary still shares the same object cache. This is an intentional interactive convenience with an insufficient verification boundary.
findings.recommendation: Make verification/package/test profiles require -Strict and carry a source/flags/compiler/object manifest. Keep an explicit interactive fallback switch with a visible degraded label that capture/report tools reject.
findings.title: Default simulator builds can succeed with old code after a source compile failure
findings.trigger: Edit a source with an existing cached object so it fails to compile; run the documented default sim/nos_build.ps1 without -Strict, then use that binary for a regression capture.
findings.verification: Build control flow and downstream invocation profiles inspected; no shared simulator build performed.

evidence.detail: Fixed TEMP/nos_cost_verify directory is reused.
Reference gfx/font/sprite are fetched from HEAD.
Both compiler calls and executable invocations proceed to hash comparison without LASTEXITCODE checks.
Only hashes of the named output files gate success; freshness is not checked.
--accuracy exit code is not checked before later success paths.
Workspace recovery instructions explicitly state that HEAD predates the intended source.

findings.impact: The reference is git HEAD, which predates recovered rendering changes, rather than the same current source with hooks disabled. GCC, git show, executables and final --accuracy have no explicit exit-code gates in the Verify block; existing equal a.bin/b.bin can survive a failed run and produce a misleading pass. Fixed nos_cost_verify and shared object caches also permit interference between runs.
findings.recommendation: Compare the same snapshotted current sources compiled with/without hooks; use a GUID temp directory, remove/avoid preexisting outputs, require successful exit codes and exact output sizes, and carry both source hashes into the verification report.
findings.title: Simulator -Verify compares against stale HEAD and does not gate native command failures
findings.trigger: Run -Verify in this recovered dirty workspace, or repeat verification after a compiler/executable fails when old outputs remain in its fixed temporary directory.
findings.verification: Static control-flow proof. Stale-output false-pass scenario was not executed; the pixel-difference assertion itself is not claimed to be wrong.

evidence.detail: Copies flash-package.ps1 into the distributed flash.ps1 and README directs users to it.
Direct esptool reset/write begins without checkpoint or range preflight.
Supported updater first waits for a checked NOSPREFS flush acknowledgment.
Supported updater validates segment/NVS overlap before reset.
Workspace requires the checked preference-preserving update route.

findings.impact: The package correctly uses separate segments and warns against flashing the merged image over NVS, but flash-package.ps1 immediately resets/writes through esptool. It never sends prefs flush or requires stored=1/match=1, so recent authoritative SD preferences can be lost across reboot. It also lacks the checked range validation used by flash_watch. NVS preservation alone does not establish SD preference durability.
findings.recommendation: Package a common checked flasher with segment manifest validation and explicit SD checkpoint acknowledgment. Preserve the existing merged-image warning; do not substitute another checkout. Keep C143 legacy variant flashing documented separately because it uses a different runtime.
findings.title: Packaged flashing bypasses the preference checkpoint used by the supported updater
findings.trigger: Use the generated dist/v1 README and flash.ps1 to update the current1.43-B watch while runtime preferences remain dirty or SD persistence is failing.
findings.verification: Actual flash_watch range helper accepted safe synthetic ranges and rejected9000/8f80 overlaps. No serial checkpoint, esptool write or reset executed.

evidence.detail: Package copies only bootloader, partition table and app binaries.
Manifest hashes the four binary outputs; fields60-66 lack ELF/source/config identity.
Displayed version uses NOS_VERSION and __DATE__.
NOS_VERSION is hardcoded1.0.0.
Existing NOSBUILD reports app_elf_sha256, providing a useful join key.
Performance reporter already requires source_revision/tree_sha256/firmware_elf_sha256 identity.

findings.impact: The package records binary hashes and honest hardware-evidence matches, but omits watchfw.elf/map, sdkconfig/dependency lock, current source manifest/archive and compiler identity. About only shows hardcoded1.0.0 plus compile date; serial info can report the ELF hash but the matching ELF is not bundled. Thus a copied image cannot independently reconstruct the changed source or symbolicate a later panic. There is no package-level feature/size-headroom gate tied to the recovered source. Root supplied an existing app headroom measurement of89888B; this report does not claim a fresh build.
findings.recommendation: Create one immutable build bundle containing ELF/map/bin/partition/config/lock/tool versions and a hash manifest of the actual dirty+untracked sources. Emit its short ID in About and trace boot metadata. Add required Solar/Orrery/Developer/home pager/sports feature checks and app-slot headroom reporting from existing build artifacts before packaging.
findings.title: Release packages omit the source identity and symbols needed to reproduce a device report
findings.trigger: Archive a dist/v1 package, flash it, continue editing this dirty recovered workspace, then investigate a crash or performance capture weeks later.
findings.verification: Package outputs, About fields and serial/report identity contracts inspected. No firmware build or symbolication performed; canonical OBS-001 covers missing crash PC/backtrace collection.

evidence.detail: Firmware instructions explicitly select committed HEAD in an external clean worktree.
HEAD predates recovered work and dirty/untracked source must be preserved.
Main simulator quick start selects sim/build.ps1.
Legacy simulator source collection includes core/apps.
Current NOS simulator compiles nos plus selected retained core services.

findings.impact: NOS.md describes a build/build_lead.ps1 route that builds committed HEAD in A:/makerspace/nos-lead and flashes it, directly conflicting with the authoritative dirty-workspace recovery instructions. README defaults to sim/build.ps1, which compiles core/apps and sim.exe rather than the current NOS simulator. Developers can validate or flash the wrong UI/source state despite following project documentation.
findings.recommendation: Make one active quick start point to tools/build.ps1 and sim/nos_build.ps1 -Strict, with dirty-source manifest and checked flashing. Mark old core/apps simulation and historical clean-HEAD instructions as archived. Crosslink the authoritative recovery/settings contract. PLAT-019 owns broader stale hardware/storage prose.
findings.title: Current setup docs still direct users to stale-HEAD firmware and the dormant simulator
findings.trigger: Follow the NOS firmware instructions at docs/NOS.md57, or README simulator commands at112, in this recovered workspace.
findings.verification: Read-only documentation and both source manifests compared; none of the documented flash/build routes was executed.

evidence.detail: Runs test_optimizations first, then its explicitly listed native suites.
Final launcher gate invokes the legacy launcher runner.
Python discovery uses test_nos_*.py, then explicit selected patterns47.
Separate strict simulator/unit/recovery/export/UI runner exists.
Separate missing/include/recursive/damage script-integrity runner exists.

findings.impact: The aggregate calls optimizations and legacy/core suites, but does not call test_workouts.ps1 or test_sim_script_io.py. Optimization discovery is limited to test_nos_*.py plus selected named files; newer test_watchctl/test_sdsync/test_imu_audit/test_watch_power_analysis and workout export tests require separate profiles. test_launcher.ps1 validates the dormant core launcher baseline while current NOS has different launcher tests. No checked-in CI workflow was found. A green partial gate therefore leaves concrete independently runnable suites uncovered. Canonical TEST-001 separately owns the currently broken SD lease fixture that blocks the aggregate.
findings.recommendation: Publish a machine-readable test matrix for active NOS, Sports/recorder/storage, host tools, pixel/model and optional hardware jobs; have one strict aggregate invoke all required offline groups and summarize skips. Use isolated GUID outputs, pin tool versions, gate source/fixture manifests and run that same profile in CI. Keep legacy coverage clearly labeled.
findings.title: Regression entry points do not define one complete current-runtime gate
findings.trigger: Run tools/test.ps1 expecting all current Sports, script-input integrity and host transport regressions before approving a change.
findings.verification: Runner reachability and tests inventory inspected. Selected developer/diagnostic/backup tests ran; full aggregate intentionally not rerun or rebuilt. Absence of .github was checked; external CI remains unknown.

evidence.detail: Untrusted RTC path sets time to epoch0 instead of fabricating a date.
Datetime validator rejects years below2000.
Invalid date is logged and returns without changing clock.
SET retains current date and replaces only time fields.
App always success-feedbacks, toasts TIME SET and pops after void HAL call.

findings.impact: board_restore_clock explicitly sets epoch0, yielding year1970. The UI preserves that date and edits only hour/minute. Firmware hal_set_datetime rejects years outside2000..2099, but its void API gives no result and the UI unconditionally shows TIME SET/success and exits. The time remains unset, leaving alarms/day grouping unreliable until an external full-date sync. The missing date entry is a feature limitation; the false success is a reachable bug.
findings.recommendation: Return a checked clock-set result; show failure/DATE NOT SET and keep the editor open when the calendar is invalid. Provide a full-date setup or clearly direct users to phone/Wi-Fi setup. Extend simulation to enforce the firmware validator.
findings.title: Set time claims success when the unset calendar makes the HAL reject the update
findings.trigger: Boot with an unset/untrusted RTC and no network/phone clock, open Settings > Set time, choose an hour/minute and tap SET.
findings.verification: manual_time_unset_date.log:actual time_input plus production board validator rejects1970 while app pops and emits TIME SET. HAL rejection is modeled using its inspected validation rule; no clock/device changed.

evidence.detail: N.sw is an array index; N.out_i is also explicitly an index at line135.
Arrival handling refreshes count/layout but does not rebase or cancel active swipe/out index ownership.
Gesture release copies N.sw to N.out_i without capturing the stable notification ID.
dismiss_flying fetches and dismisses whatever currently occupies N.out_i at lines200/205.
Notification posts prepend using memmove; service dismiss sends the current item ID at line225.
Observed target_id=-6 incoming_id=-7 target_retained=1 incoming_retained=0 remaining=2.

findings.impact: The incoming notification is removed while the originally swiped notification remains. For phone-origin notifications the service can send DISMISS for the wrong ID.
findings.recommendation: Capture a stable ID when a press/swipe begins; resolve that ID immediately before any action. Freeze or cancel the visual owner if it disappears. Rebase geometry on every store revision, including updates/full-capacity replacements where count is unchanged.
findings.title: Incoming notifications can change the target of an active swipe dismissal
findings.trigger: Start swiping notification at index 0; release it into fly-out, then post a new notification before the old card crosses the removal threshold. Updates that move an existing ID to the front can also shift indexes, even with unchanged count.
findings.verification: Reproduced using current sys_notifs.c and current engine with real local notification-store operations; see audit_repro.c and run_repro.py. Add cases for arrival before release, arrival during fly-out, same-count update/capacity replacement and selected-ID removal.

evidence.detail: Animation time is stored as global float.
nos_dt is computed from elapsed_ms, then directly accumulated into nos_t at line2242 without an epoch/precision policy.
Authored frame count is derived from float nos_t minus float origin; tween progress uses the same difference at line327.
Touch long-press recognition compares the affected clock against P.t_down.
Existing clock test intentionally resets to a small origin at line58, so it does not cover uptime precision loss.
Current-engine test observed CLOCK origin=524288 requested=.025 actual=.000000000 while dt=.025000000.

findings.impact: Animations/deadlines drift well before the final freeze. At the freeze, frame count and nos_dt still advance but nos_t-based tweens, long press, toast/banner timeouts and power-sheet deadlines can stop completing. Wall uptime to encounter this depends on active/AOD/sleep frame cadence;524288 seconds is a clock value, not a claimed six-day wall-clock soak.
findings.recommendation: Represent monotonic animation deadlines with an integer64-bit clock and convert bounded relative intervals to float, or otherwise establish a consistent precision-preserving timestamp API. Merely changing the accumulator to double while leaving every app t0 as float does not solve relative-time precision.
findings.title: Unbounded float animation time drifts and eventually stops advancing at ordinary cadence
findings.trigger: Accumulate a large active animation-clock origin. At nos_t=65536 seconds,25ms advances by23.4375ms; at131072 and262144 seconds it advances by31.25ms. At524288 seconds a25ms frame advances by0.
findings.verification: Current nos.c privately compiled and executed; injected five large origins and called real nos_frame_run(25). Keep these origins in a regression and verify tween, long-press and timeout completion at each.

evidence.detail: Settings benchmark p95_ms42,p99_ms44; deadline125/222 frames in the artifact.
Launcher benchmark p95_ms38,p99_ms44; deadline184/224 frames in the artifact.
Validation explicitly records approximation, unmet hard floor and absence of optical/long-duration measurements.
NOS_MIN_FPS is30; default target cadence is40.
Extra icon interpolation cost is estimated rather than target-calibrated.
Shutter cost accounting is explicitly a placeholder mask-class estimate, not measured target cost.

findings.impact: The saved target benchmark reports Apps p95=38ms,p99=44ms and Settings p95=42ms,p99=44ms; both exceed a33.33ms frame floor. The audit did not repeat target measurements and does not assign the entire overrun to blur alone.
findings.recommendation: Profile these exact windows on the target using tick, record, CPU raster, stripe wait, history and native blend areas. Optimize or bound the dominant measured owner; retain pixel-reference controls and report quality/approximation separately from frame-floor attainment.
findings.title: Measured Apps and Settings scrolling still fail the 30 FPS hard floor
findings.trigger: Scroll the integrated Apps page or Settings during the existing continuous-trail target benchmark windows.
findings.verification: Existing flash-validation artifact reviewed as supplied evidence;41 independent current-source host regressions passed, which establish functional coverage rather than target frame rate.

evidence.detail: Pattern rebuild key is only hour*60+minute; neither hour24 nor resulting digit strings are compared.
Stale return copies now to prev without recomputing now.
Reachable 24-hour clock toggle.
Home reveal does not call face.enter to invalidate MATRIX.

findings.verification: Actual-source host repro observed unchanged pattern after toggle and correct rebuild after advancing to 13:38; checks/faces/matrix-contract-repro.log.

evidence.detail: Face context explicitly receives weather temp_c.
S.temp is copied directly from temp_c.
TMP formats S.temp without units_metric conversion.
Weather converts to Fahrenheit when units_metric is false.
User Units control toggles units_metric.

findings.recommendation: Use the same temperature conversion/rounding helper as Weather and include a C/F cue where practical.
findings.title: SPLIT temperature ignores the Imperial unit preference
findings.trigger: Enable Imperial units with valid weather and select SPLIT.
findings.verification: Source call chain and reachable Settings control verified; no runtime temperature sensor claim.

evidence.detail: active_min >0 is used as availability; zero becomes steps/110.
Authoritative active_min is the saved cadence-counted value, including zero.
Active minutes increment only on the cadence condition.

findings.recommendation: Use the authoritative active_min unconditionally, or add a separate explicit validity flag if estimated mode is needed.
findings.title: SEGMENT replaces a valid zero active-minute total with a step estimate
