findings.verification: Actual-source host repro passed with service active_min=0/displayed10; checks/faces/segment-contract-repro.log.

evidence.detail: Denied mx_state allocation exits build.
draw returns immediately without fallback time.
No time drawn until s_font.ok.
A denied glyph leaves scaled font unfinished and retryable.
Denied main state allocation returns false.
draw returns immediately when mandatory state is unavailable.

findings.impact: MATRIX returns no drawing commands; Orrery returns before drawing its clock; SEGMENT draws rings/data but draw_time returns without time. The shell still draws its own overlays, so this is loss of the face clock rather than a claimed whole-panel hang.
findings.recommendation: Render a small allocation-free clock and an optional availability cue until required state/fonts are ready; keep the existing retry and ownership behavior.
findings.title: Several watch faces lose their basic clock when face/font allocation is denied
findings.trigger: Select MATRIX or Orrery before its mandatory state can be allocated, or select SEGMENT while a scaled-font glyph allocation remains denied.
findings.verification: MATRIX mandatory-allocation denial observed zero commands in isolated host test. SEGMENT/Orrery variants are source-proven guard paths, not separately injected current-device failures.

evidence.detail: Both ASSET_OK and ASSET_FAILED are adopted; only cancellation is excluded.
Failure clears tex_ok but stage still increments at712.
stage>=3 exits permanently.
PHOTO remains selected; LOADING only depends on stage<3.
Missing texture silently substitutes ob_tint.

findings.impact: Failure adopts the returned buffers, advances stage and eventually removes LOADING. PHOTO renders a tinted fallback indefinitely until body reset/reopen, with no failure cue or retry.
findings.recommendation: Track failed stages distinctly, show PHOTO UNAVAILABLE/fallback state and retry on explicit action or bounded SD-ready recovery without violating page ownership.
findings.title: A failed card photo load never retries after the SD asset becomes available
findings.trigger: Open a texture-backed card with absent/unreadable file or SD; let the failure complete; restore the valid asset while leaving that body open.
findings.verification: Actual-source host repro: missing Sun asset -> stage3/tex0; create valid1048576-byte asset -> still stage3/tex0 after200 load/poll iterations; checks/faces/card-asset-retry-repro.log.

evidence.detail: Initial estimate and8 unconstrained Newton iterations; no residual/convergence failure return.
Cached elliptic conic path consumes this solver.
Public elliptic conic path consumes the same solver.
Preview fallback can call the same exact solver.
Actual Lemmon catalog record has e=0.9955,q=0.53,tp=2460988.04.
Face evaluates this actual comet through cached/preview conic path.
Separate float belt solver stops after3 Newton steps with no residual check.
Actual belt index3020 has e=0.993 and mean anomaly0.1degrees near pack epoch.

findings.impact: The8-step Newton solve can diverge and still feed sin/cos and visible positions. Actual source returns E=-1963363234.2687581 with residual1963363235.2327611rad; public and cached radius68.681648957AU differs from monotone-bisection solution28.512007850AU. Reduced residual0.1747377508rad and3D position separation40.455233130AU exclude an equivalent extra-revolution alias. A separate actual-face probe of its3-iteration belt solve at2026-10-21 (JD2461334.5), index3020/e≈0.993, differs by9.025477 projected pixels in BEYOND from a bracketed solve using the same basis. These are numerical failures, independent of external ephemeris accuracy;9px is a host source result, not a device measurement.
findings.recommendation: Use convergent safeguarded solvers or validate residual and fall back for both double conics and the separate float belt path; add actual high-e catalog cases across supported dates and exact/preview parity with an independent solution.
findings.title: Kepler solvers return incorrect positions for bundled high-eccentricity bodies
findings.trigger: Travel to dates such as JD2465445.0 (2038-01-21 12:00 UTC) for the bundled C/2025 A6 (Lemmon), e=0.9955. This lies inside the documented planet-model date range.
findings.verification: Compiled actual core/ephem.c with actual catalog; independent monotone bisection comparison, reduced residual and public/cached position checks in checks/faces/ephem-residual-repro.log. Separately compiled actual face_orrery.c and compared belt_exact to a bracketed solution using the identical basis/projection in checks/faces/belt-residual-repro.log. Existing ephem_test still passes.

evidence.detail: Only face tick advances ep_scan_step4 days.
Unlocked chip opens the Events screen without checking scan completion.
Row build is called only on enter.
Events tick only advances list animation.
Once transition ends, only top screen ticks.

findings.impact: The list stays incomplete for the entire visit. No scan owner runs behind the top Events screen and its rows only build at enter. Returning HOME resumes the scan; reopening is required to see new results.
findings.recommendation: Give scanning a service/Events owner with bounded slices, publish a stable generation and rebuild rows when complete/progress changes; expose progress so early results are understandable.
findings.title: Opening Events freezes a partially completed astronomy scan and row list
findings.trigger: Open the Events chip while Orrery is still scanning its460-day window; the chip can appear after the first qualifying events, before completion.
findings.verification: Real engine probe observed20 scan events/16 visible rows unchanged through200 top-screen frames; returning HOME completed to27 events; checks/faces/events-lifecycle-repro.log.

evidence.detail: Model declares Table1 valid1800-2050.
Year ring lap is12*365.25 days.
Ring taps form an unrestricted target date.
Ring/TIME drag adds unrestricted days.
Momentum also advances unrestricted offset.
Event jump accepts unrestricted JD.

findings.impact: Planet/event/card calculations keep presenting ordinary precise-looking results outside the Table1 interval declared by ephem.h. This audit does not quantify the error outside that interval.
findings.recommendation: Clamp to a documented supported range or visibly label extrapolation and stop accuracy-sensitive event/card claims outside it.
findings.title: Orrery time travel silently exceeds its declared ephemeris validity interval
findings.trigger: Continue turning the year ring or use fast TIME travel until before1800 or after2050; only a few12-year ring turns are needed from2026.
findings.verification: Complete time-input, momentum, jump and render callers inspected; no external accuracy assertion or extreme-date hardware test.

evidence.detail: Active tick calls cache_init then full fk_sfont_build.
Full builder loops all remaining glyphs.
Cold cache allocates4sprites and initializes row spans.
Active cold path calls cold_track(NRING*NSEG), not WARM_SEGS.
Background warm path normally limits glyph/track work per frame.

findings.impact: A single UI tick can finish all remaining scaled glyphs, allocate/initialize4 quadrant sprites, compute per-row ring spans and raster all180 empty segments before rendering. This stacks unbounded cold work on an interactive frame; current board deadline impact was not measured.
findings.recommendation: Retain bounded preparation on visible cold entry and draw a basic clock/ring fallback while it completes; qualify cold entry separately from warmed steady-state.
findings.title: SEGMENT cold entry synchronously completes work that background preparation normally slices
findings.trigger: Select/preview SEGMENT soon after startup, before its background font/ring warm-up completes, or after warm-up was delayed by allocation pressure.
findings.verification: Code path and warm/cold guards inspected; performance risk is strong inference, not a new measured30-FPS failure.

evidence.detail: sample_ms advances only after a successful nonempty FIFO acquisition.
hal_hr_get returns sensor presence and the cached H->cur, without an age filter.
Presence is taken from hal_hr_get; 624 sets fresh=1 without checking sample_ms or acquisition identity.
Contact/good times accumulate UI dt from repeated cached values; 637 locks after the elapsed thresholds.
Locked BPM changes only for another positive value; 651 similarly retains SpO2 when the new value is zero.
Leaving records H.bpm_shown/H.spo2; svc_heart_record at svc.c571 stamps the current epoch.

findings.impact: One old acquisition can satisfy two seconds of contact and lock a current-looking BPM. Once locked, zero/unavailable BPM and SpO2 do not clear the displayed values while contact remains true. Leaving records the retained BPM with the current wall-clock time.
findings.recommendation: Track acquisition timestamps and age independently from attachment/contact. Count lock duration only across fresh acceptable samples; distinguish last reading from live value and clear or label invalid BPM and SpO2. Record the actual accepted acquisition time.
findings.title: Heart live display treats a cached reading as fresh and can retain invalidated values as current
findings.trigger: The HR strap remains present and hal_hr_get keeps returning its cached struct after FIFO acquisition stops; alternatively, a locked reading is followed by on_wrist=true with bpm/SpO2 becoming unavailable or low quality.
findings.verification: Source-traced against the HAL cache contract and the workout recorder freshness guard at workout.c280-302. Isolated cache observation proves a getter can provide one unchanged acquisition repeatedly; the full rendered Heart state machine was not executed by this audit.

evidence.detail: hr_sample checks presence, on_wrist, BPM range and quality only; 172 increments sum and count for every call.
INTRO samples HR every tick; SESSION does so at 310.
Completion averages the per-frame count, then svc_heart_record at 334 assigns a current reading timestamp.

findings.impact: The summary average can be based entirely on an old reading and is weighted by render-frame polling frequency rather than accepted acquisition time. It is then recorded as a new current reading.
findings.recommendation: Accept only new, in-session, age-bounded acquisitions; accumulate a declared time-weighted average with valid coverage and show unavailable when coverage is insufficient. Preserve sample-time provenance when recording the result.
findings.title: Breathe averages repeated cached HR values without age or acquisition checks
findings.trigger: A breathing session polls an attached strap whose last cached HR is still on_wrist/quality-valid, including an acquisition from before the session or after a FIFO stall. UI frame cadence varies.
findings.verification: checks/health/checks.json hr_cache_observation: actual extracted hr_sample accepted100calls with identical sample_ms=1, average123.0. This reproduces the acceptance defect, not physiological accuracy.

evidence.detail: hist_push stores only a BPM byte; no timestamp is retained.
First background collection is scheduled two minutes after boot, rather than aligned to local ten-minute slots.
heart_tick fetches the existing ring; 560 calculates last epoch from current ep and array position.
Any later calculated epoch replaces bpm_last_epoch, even if no history sample arrived.
Widget formats age from last_epoch and labels it JUST NOW for age<90 seconds at 947.

findings.impact: The latest nonzero reading repeatedly becomes new again; the Home widget can report JUST NOW indefinitely for an unchanged old sample. Chart/day/minimum assumptions also cannot reliably reflect actual 10-minute acquisition times or gaps.
findings.recommendation: Return sample timestamps or a timestamped history generation from HAL. Update last-reading time only when an acquisition arrives; bin actual timestamps and explicitly represent gaps and reboot retention boundaries.
findings.title: Heart history fabricates acquisition times from the current clock
findings.trigger: heart_tick runs again with the same unchanged HAL history, or background samples were delayed/missing. The ring carries BPM bytes but no acquisition timestamps.
findings.verification: checks/health/checks.json/hr_cache_observation: extracted actual heart_tick with one unchanged history byte advanced bpm_last_epoch from1792497600 to1792498200 when only wall-clock time moved600 seconds.

evidence.detail: Each workout heart sampling call enables the single shared stream; regular metrics are SAMPLE_MS=1000.
A normal Heart leave calls hal_hr_enable(0) regardless of an active workout.
hr_stop calls the same global disable; session completion invokes it at332.
hal_hr_enable overwrites one enabled flag with no owner or reference count.
want is enabled||bg;234 stops a running sensor if false;233 restarts when wanted again.

findings.impact: The strap service can stop the sensor and reset its DSP on restart even though the workout still needs it, creating avoidable HR coverage/reacquisition gaps. The exact interruption duration depends on task timing; it was not measured on hardware.
findings.recommendation: Use per-consumer leases for workout, Heart, Breathe and background HR. Releasing one lease should not stop a sensor needed by another; log transitions with active owner bits and reason.
findings.title: Closing Heart or Breathe can disable HR still requested by a background workout
findings.trigger: An active workout is sampling HR at up to1Hz while the user leaves Heart or completes/leaves Breathe. The external task observes enabled=0 before the next workout enable, and no background collection is active.
findings.verification: Reachable source schedule verified. No task-interleaving or physical HR gap measurement was performed; assessed as strong inference rather than an observed device failure.

evidence.detail: call_reveal sets s_revealing and re-invokes enter.
init unconditionally memset clears the shared E state and sets defaults.
Energy/Battery/Logs enter callbacks always init; report_enter46 and tune_enter51 do likewise without nos_revealed guards.
Every report_enter immediately calls sports_report with outcome -1.

findings.impact: Date, zoom, selection and unsaved editor/report choices are discarded. Quick Report also writes another unlabelled time mark on each uncover, so one visit can create unintended duplicate markers.
findings.recommendation: Honor reveal semantics and retain per-screen editing/timeline state. Separate first-open actions from uncover callbacks, and emit an automatic time mark only for an explicit new report session.
findings.title: Energy-family screens reset context on uncover and Quick Report emits an extra mark
findings.trigger: A sheet, pushed child screen or other cover is closed, causing nos call_reveal to invoke the underlying Energy-family enter callback. This includes Energy food/water entry or a partially configured Quick Report.
findings.verification: checks/health/energy_reenter.json: actual extracted refresh/init/energy_enter/report_enter callbacks. Reenter clears day-4/300..600/editor777 to day0/0..1440/editorclosed/250 and produces a second time mark while resetting report choices. This is callback-level testing, not a complete GUI run.

evidence.detail: RESET discards tuning_adjust(0,0) return value and always displays success.
Checked persistence failure returns0 before cfg is assigned at39.

findings.impact: The UI announces DEFAULT THRESHOLDS RESTORED although tuning_adjust returns failure before installing the default configuration; active thresholds remain unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Branch on the checked return value as the sensitivity controls already do; retain a retryable failure message and display the active configuration revision.
findings.title: Wrist Tuning reports defaults restored even when the checked save failed
findings.trigger: The user taps RESET while hal_store_save_checked fails because storage is unavailable or rejects the write.
findings.verification: Source-proven checked return/control-flow mismatch. No device save failure was induced. Existing engine tests do not cover this app action.

evidence.detail: The loop includes seven bars but425 only sums v!=0 and i<6.
Denominator is the number of nonzero prior-day totals.
The visible heading is THIS WEEK,496 DAILY AVG.
week[0..5] are previous rolling days;403 makes index6 current, not a calendar-week boundary.

findings.impact: The value labelled THIS WEEK / DAILY AVG is an average of positive previous-day totals only. A single12000-step prior day plus five genuine zero days reports12000 rather than a six-day2000 average; today can show activity while the average remains empty/zero.
findings.recommendation: Define and label the intended rolling or calendar window. Track missing-day validity separately from genuine zero and use all valid days in the denominator; explicitly decide whether today participates.
findings.title: Activity DAILY AVG excludes every zero-step day and the displayed current day
findings.trigger: The rolling seven-day chart contains genuine zero-step days, or today is the only day with steps.
findings.verification: Exact denominator and labels inspected. Arithmetic example follows the actual loop; no full-app render test or historical zero-day fixture was run.

evidence.detail: act_save calls void hal_store_save at448, then always clears s_as_dirty and advances the save time at449-450.
Day rollover uses that unchecked save.
Periodic saves are gated on s_as_dirty, so a failure with no later change is not retried.
The storage API exposes hal_store_save_checked for callers needing a verified result.

findings.impact: Hourly bins, prior-day totals or active minutes can be lost, and the failed state is no longer scheduled for retry. This caller-level issue is distinct from the storage implementation failures STOR-001..003.
findings.recommendation: Use the checked result, keep dirty state on failure and retry with bounded backoff. Log key, day, error and last successful checkpoint time, separating persisted and RAM activity status.
findings.title: Activity history clears its dirty flag after an unchecked failed save
findings.trigger: A nosact save at rollover or the ten-minute maintenance interval fails, then no new step/active-minute change marks the data dirty before reset.
findings.verification: Source-proven unconditional dirty-clear path. No hardware failure injection was performed for nosact; unrelated storage test results are not claimed as this caller test.

evidence.detail: workout_init returns immediately after initialized has been set once.
Writer memory uses heap_caps_calloc;700 sets initialized=1 before allocation is checked.
Allocation failure returns with ioNULL.
Task creation failure increments errors and frees/clears io; no retry path follows.
Storage service returns when ioNULL;729 start requires storage.ready.

findings.impact: initialized is already true and io remainsNULL, so future init/tick/storage calls never retry. storage.ready staysfalse, preventing new workouts for the remainder of the boot even if memory later becomes available.
findings.recommendation: Expose a distinct worker-initialization error, retain retryable state and retry allocation/task creation at bounded intervals or on an explicit action. Do not start a workout until durable storage is ready.
findings.title: One workout writer allocation or task-creation failure disables Sports storage until reboot
findings.trigger: At first initialization, the PSRAM writer-memory allocation or PSRAM-backed task creation fails transiently.
findings.verification: ESP-only source paths and guards inspected; host tests use static writer memory and cannot validate FreeRTOS allocation failure or recovery.

evidence.detail: history_refresh reads only the current in-memory count and entries.
With zero entries, history_draw unconditionally renders No sessions yet at869.
workout_storage_status exposes ready, available, corrupt, foreign and errors for distinguishing states.
An unreadable/invalid bank pair can leave load incomplete; storage.corrupt is retained at679.

findings.impact: The UI says No sessions yet / Finish a Sports session even when it has not established that history is empty. The storage layer preserves corrupt banks and exposes ready/corrupt/available, but that distinction is lost on this page.
findings.recommendation: Use storage status for loading/unavailable/corrupt/original-card-required states; show empty history only after a successful authoritative load. Offer retry and a concise diagnostic reason.
findings.title: Empty workout history hides loading, unavailable and corrupt-card states
findings.trigger: The user opens Recent Workouts before asynchronous history load completes, or while no history is loaded because the card is unavailable, unreadable or corrupt.
findings.verification: Source-traced getter/UI branch with explicit storage guards. No live card removal, corruption injection on device, or GUI replay was performed.

evidence.detail: execute uses uncorrelated DONE completion.
GET retries TimeoutError but not typed command-input rejection.
Capability probing can raise on an explicit ERR response.
Checkpoint logic is separately implemented without a shared reply guard.

findings.impact: Different tools retry, stop or wait for different timeouts; a successful navigation can appear failed, an explicit rejected SD command can wait 60s, and operators need bespoke guard/resynchronization code.
findings.recommendation: Create one tested transport library with capability negotiation, command IDs, explicit dispatch/result ACKs and per-command idempotence metadata; centralize guarded read-only retries and preserve no-blind-retry behavior for recording/reset/delete actions. Export raw wire diagnostics with redaction.
findings.title: Host tools lack one consistent command/reply and rejected-input recovery contract
findings.trigger: USB input rejection or a lost DONE occurs during watchctl, flash checkpointing, SD capability probing or scripted QA.
findings.verification: Observed previous smoke timed out at HOME and capability reads hit ERR command input. Existing host mocks pass their covered scenarios; audit SD lease test currently fails to compile because its do_get2 mock is stale.

evidence.detail: Defined persistent events store reset context and three integers but no crash payload/core dump record.
Boot capture stores reset reason and recent RTC events.
Current layout has no dedicated crash/core-dump partition.

findings.impact: The next boot identifies a crash and replays recent actions, but cannot attribute the actual exception or stack to an app/worker. This limits diagnosis of the reported recording and Battery History crashes.
findings.recommendation: Add a bounded crash artifact containing build ID, reset cause, exception PC/address, core/task, SP and a supported backtrace/core-dump format. Reserve retention separately from ordinary journal rotation and export symbolized reports using the matching ELF.
findings.title: Persistent crash records do not preserve the faulting instruction, task or backtrace
findings.trigger: A panic/watchdog reset occurs and the USB serial log was not captured.
findings.verification: Source/schema/layout review. Two prior panic boots were recorded during debug activities; their exact causes were not established. Do not re-label all historical boot IDs as crashes.

evidence.detail: Hook records sequence, size, capability and API function string only.
Periodic heap sample covers general internal heap every 30s, without DMA-specific minimum or failure correlation.

findings.impact: NOSALLOC retains only the latest size/caps/function label and counters. Function heap_caps_malloc identifies the allocator rather than the requesting subsystem, so later free-memory reports cannot explain the failure.
findings.recommendation: Use a small allocation-failure ring in internal/RTC memory with monotonic timestamp, core/task ID, bounded return address/callsite token, caps and nearby free/largest metrics captured only when safe. Persist/translate outside the hook; track resource owner high-water marks.
findings.title: Allocation diagnostics lack timestamps and allocating callsite context
findings.trigger: A transient internal/DMA allocation fails between sparse snapshots.
findings.verification: Observed last flash diagnostics contain over 1,000 repeated size512 caps0x8 failures but no time/caller. Hook changes must preserve ISR/cache-disabled safety and be verified on Xtensa.

evidence.detail: QUEUE_CAP128 and RETAIN_CAP32 bound retention.
Overflow drops new queue events.
Diagnostic service is called from the shared sports writer worker.
Persistence requires the same SD lease/lock.

findings.impact: The 128-record diagnostic queue fills and drops new records; a 32-entry RTC ring retains only a recent suffix. Action/power history around a prolonged incident can disappear, just when it is needed most.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize fault/power/recording-transition events over routine events, reserve an emergency bounded channel independent of SD, record first/last/count summaries for repeated failures, and expose a sticky evidence-loss indication with an export bundle.
findings.title: Diagnostic evidence shares the failing SD resource and can overflow before recovery
findings.trigger: SD allocation/I/O failures stop the sports writer and the diagnostic consumer for minutes.
findings.verification: Observed pre-flash NOSLOG showed available0, queue128, >500 dropped and >4,000 storage errors. Current flash recovered this temporarily; longer-term retention behavior is not fixed.

evidence.detail: One timestamp is captured before all seven sequential services.
ext_idle uses unsigned (now-last)>NOS_EXT_IDLE_MS.
GPS stops on that idle result; getter renews last_get at line 301.
LTE want_on uses the same helper; getters renew last_get at lines 407/420.
HR disables its user stream on this result; getter renews at line 306.

findings.impact: Unsigned now-last_get becomes nearly UINT32_MAX and passes the 8-second idle test. GPS, LTE, or HR can stop while a visible app or workout is renewing them; subsequent enables may restart them. A slow preceding service widens the timing window.
findings.recommendation: Use a wrap-safe signed elapsed comparison that treats a renewal newer than the captured time as fresh; synchronize lease state and refresh the service timestamp around potentially slow work.
findings.title: Concurrent getter renewal can immediately expire an external sensor lease
findings.trigger: The ext task captures now, then the UI renews last_get at a later millisecond before the task tests that lease.
findings.verification: Actual ext_idle/ext_due helper text was extracted unchanged and compiled. now=10000,last=10001 produced idle=1 although a renewed lease requires 0. Ordinary fresh, expired, and rollover controls behaved as expected; see checks/platform/lease_edge.json.

evidence.detail: Background flag is set by the periodic scheduler.
A retained bg flag restarts a stopped device.
Pointer failures stop after ten errors but do not clear bg.
FIFO payload failure returns before timeout evaluation.
BG_MAX_MS and contact-loss checks are inside the successful nonempty FIFO branch.
Getter copies cache without age invalidation.
Workout accepts HR only with quality/range and sample_ms freshness gates.

findings.impact: The advertised 40-second background limit is checked only after a successful nonempty FIFO read. The LED stream can remain requested indefinitely; pointer failures call stop but leave bg set, causing another start. Old cached readings can also remain visible to callers that do not inspect sample_ms. Workout metrics explicitly check the 3-second freshness limit, reducing that consumer impact.
findings.recommendation: Apply the background deadline before any acquisition early return, cap restart attempts, clear acquisition state on persistent errors, and invalidate stale cached outputs consistently.
findings.title: Heart-rate background sampling has no effective timeout when FIFO acquisition fails
findings.trigger: A background MAX30102 measurement starts, then its FIFO remains empty, FIFO payload reads fail, or repeated pointer reads fail.
findings.verification: Reachable state-machine review; existing host suite does not inject MAX30102 FIFO or bus faults. Measure LED current and recovery on hardware with a controlled sensor fault.

evidence.detail: Trigger-write failures increment errors and return without invalidating cur.
Only a later data-read failure branch invalidates after the error threshold.
Skipped conversions also return without invalidation or age tracking.
Getter returns the cached validity without an age check.

findings.impact: The old pressure, temperature and humidity remain valid indefinitely. Weather/altimeter UI and logs can present frozen measurements as current; no acquisition timestamp is in hal_env.
findings.recommendation: Track last successful acquisition and invalidate by age across trigger, readiness and data-read failure paths; expose the last operation/error and retry count.
findings.title: Environment cache remains valid through repeated conversion-trigger failures
findings.trigger: The BME/BMP driver has a valid sample, then forced-mode trigger writes fail repeatedly, or reads repeatedly return the skipped/not-ready sentinel.
findings.verification: Source-proven retention path; no sensor fault injection performed.

evidence.detail: Only status-read failures advance the invalidation threshold.
Status success clears errors before channel reads.
Failed/not-ready ALS data preserves the copied cache.
Copied validity is republished regardless of fresh channels.
Automatic brightness trusts hal_light_get and l.valid.

findings.impact: The error counter resets after the status read, then the previous valid lux is republished. Automatic brightness can remain based on a frozen reading indefinitely. Proximity has the same missing acquisition-age distinction.
findings.recommendation: Track ALS/proximity success timestamps and channel errors independently, expire old channels, and expose stale/invalid state to automatic brightness.
findings.title: Light cache can remain valid when measurement-channel reads cease succeeding
findings.trigger: APDS status reads continue succeeding, but ALS data reads fail or never become ready after an earlier valid reading.
findings.verification: Source review; APDS hardware disconnect/channel-fault behavior remains untested.

evidence.detail: Shutdown only checks the IMU recorder and IMU browser.
Then calls board_prepare_sleep and esp_deep_sleep_start.
Preparation stops board/assets, unmounts SD and disables the onboard IMU; no external shutdown hook.
GPS backup requires an explicit UART command; no power gate wire.
LTE power-off is an asynchronous multi-step AT/key state machine.
HR shutdown is an explicit register write from the ext service.

findings.impact: The ESP enters deep sleep after stopping the board task and onboard IMU, but external device shutdown commands and file-close services have no completion barrier. VBAT-powered strap devices can continue consuming power after the UI says power off. Exact residual current depends on attached hardware and GPIO behavior and was not measured. Audio file ownership is also being reviewed independently by root.
findings.recommendation: Add an asynchronous platform shutdown coordinator: reject new work, stop each external stream, wait for owned files and hardware acknowledgments with bounded failure reporting, then unmount and sleep.
findings.title: Power-off does not coordinate shutdown of optional strap devices
findings.trigger: The user confirms POWER OFF while optional GPS, LTE, HR or audio streams are active.
findings.verification: Call-chain review and driver power model; validate shutdown under each attached module and measure final rail current.

evidence.detail: FT3168 board_touch_read returns 0 for both failed I2C and no-contact data.
touch_poll treats the return directly as down.
Every down-state change queues a real input sample.
Actual touch driver errors are counted and the last code retained.

findings.impact: The read returns the same value as no touch. touch_poll enqueues an up event and a later successful read starts another down event, splitting a drag or completing a tap while the finger is still on the panel. Device evidence contains I2C errors, but it does not prove which gestures were affected.
findings.recommendation: Make touch acquisition tri-state (valid down/up, invalid read), retain contact briefly across invalid reads, and cancel a gesture explicitly after a bounded fault window rather than emitting a normal tap release.
findings.title: A transient touch I2C failure becomes an input release
findings.trigger: A finger is down during a temporary FT3168 I2C timeout or bus error.
findings.verification: Source-proven event transformation. Existing timeout injection and device error evidence are available; no new device interaction was performed.

evidence.detail: Touch probe plus mode write establish a one-time availability flag.
IMU probe/ID/configuration establish a one-time flag.
False touch availability short-circuits all normal reads.
False IMU availability short-circuits raw reads.
Board sampler only enters acquisition when s_imu_ok.

findings.impact: s_touch_ok/s_imu_ok remain false; normal reads return absent without retry. Touch may be unusable for the whole boot, and walking/wrist wake/raw recording remain unavailable. Optional external hot-plug support is separately a missing feature, not assumed to be promised.
findings.recommendation: Use bounded backoff reprobe/reconfiguration for essential base devices, expose a retry control and first/last error, and avoid spinning/log flooding on genuine absence.
findings.title: Transient boot probe failure disables base touch or IMU until reboot
findings.trigger: The 1.43-B touch probe/mode write or IMU ID/configuration transaction fails once at startup, then the device/bus becomes usable.
findings.verification: Code path review; base-board delayed-power-up and bus recovery require hardware validation.

evidence.detail: Clock-change callback sets pending epoch and dirty.
Control-read and stop failures return silently.
Calendar/restart failure can mark RTC invalid, but caller receives no result.
Dirty is cleared before rtc_save and never restored on failure.

findings.impact: board_task clears s_rtc_dirty before invoking a void rtc_save. Failure is not requeued, so battery-backed RTC may retain old time or invalid state until another sync or explicit sleep attempt. Early control-read/stop failures return without the RTC warning or validity update.
findings.recommendation: Return write status, retain the pending request until success with bounded retry, use current trusted UTC when retrying, and log the failed register operation and retry/recovery event.
findings.title: RTC synchronization request is discarded before the write succeeds
findings.trigger: USB/BLE/NTP sets system time, then one RTC control read, stop command, calendar write, or restart fails.
findings.verification: Source-proven loss of retry state. Portable RTC encode/decode tests passed; I2C write-failure recovery is not covered.

evidence.detail: hal_wifi_ap contains ssid[24].
Full scanned SSID is snprintf-truncated into that field.
Password flow copies the truncated scan name.
Connect submits the copied name.

findings.impact: The scan model stores only 23 visible bytes and that truncated value becomes the actual connect target. Scan selection cannot join the full-name network; Other network/phone setup can provide all 32 bytes.
findings.recommendation: Store the complete 32-byte SSID plus terminator in the HAL snapshot, preserve exact bytes for connection, and truncate only the drawn label.
findings.title: Wi-Fi scan selection loses long network names
findings.trigger: The selected network has a 24-32-byte SSID.
findings.verification: Source-proven contract truncation; no network join was attempted.

evidence.detail: Bluetooth tile state is nos_prefs.ble.
Toggle only changes the preference.
Host explicitly keeps BLE up and only applies the Wi-Fi preference.
Radio startup always invokes ble_init.
BLE connection status ignores the saved enable flag.

findings.impact: The saved/tile state changes, but NimBLE still starts and remains connectable. The control therefore cannot deliver the battery or availability behavior implied by off. Current source intentionally keeps the phone link alive, which should be represented honestly in the UI.
findings.recommendation: Implement explicit BLE enable/disable ownership and restart behavior, or replace the off toggle with a truthful supported phone-link action.
findings.title: Bluetooth off preference changes the tile without disabling the radio
findings.trigger: The user turns the Bluetooth tile off or boots with nos_prefs.ble=0.
findings.verification: End-to-end source review; parent coordinates duplicate UI findings. No live radio state was changed.

evidence.detail: Mount retry is synchronous in the same board loop as sensing.
Pedometer save and periodic board log occur before the next sensing cycle.
Board log uses synchronous fopen/fprintf/fclose and storage_status.
audio_service runs before GPS/LTE/environment/light/mag/HR on one task.
Audio playback reads SD on that service task; recording fwrite is at line 371.
Driver notes the 512-byte UART ring fills in about 44ms at 115200.
HR hardware FIFO has 32 samples at the configured 100Hz effective rate.

findings.impact: Base walking/knock/cached wake and power sampling pause behind board-task SD work. All slow strap services pause behind audio_service, risking GPS UART loss and HR FIFO overflow. The separate raw IMU sampler/writer separation protects its own stream from SD, but does not protect the board cached-motion pipeline. Delay frequency and magnitude have not been measured here.
findings.recommendation: Move filesystem operations to a dedicated bounded worker, retain mount leases/SD locking, and add loop-gap/max-I/O-duration/FIFO-overrun/serial-loss counters before drawing causal conclusions.
findings.title: Synchronous SD work shares tasks with motion and optional sensor servicing
findings.trigger: An SD operation blocks for longer than a normal acquisition period: board log/stat/close, storage retry, pedometer save, or audio_service playback/recording I/O.
findings.verification: Conditional source analysis. Existing tests verify portable algorithms, not slow-card scheduling. Replay on a controlled delayed I/O backend before hardware tests.

evidence.detail: Final DMA fence takes two credits with portMAX_DELAY.
Flush worker waits for DMA credits indefinitely.
UI raster waits for raw credit indefinitely.
frame_drain waits indefinitely for worker fence.
Separate benchmark code has an explicit DMA timeout; active NOS path does not.

findings.impact: Raw/rotated credit waits and the UI frame fence can block indefinitely, freezing UI commands, preference pumping and the UI-owned service loop. Other FreeRTOS tasks may continue. This is a recovery gap, not a claim that it caused a historical hang.
findings.recommendation: Add bounded progress monitoring and a deferred diagnostic snapshot containing queue/credit/job state; recover through an owned display reinitialization or controlled restart after preserving settings. Never return buffer ownership while DMA might still be active.
findings.title: Display DMA waits have no bounded fault or recovery path
findings.trigger: The display driver accepts a submission but an expected completion callback never returns a credit, or the flush worker stops progressing.
findings.verification: Source-proven unbounded waits conditional on a missing completion. Frame-timer failure tests passed but do not cover DMA loss.

evidence.detail: Invert/sleep/wake/brightness branch return values are ignored through line 213.
Theme state is advanced before command completion.
Brightness cache is advanced before the transaction.
Sleep state is advanced before transaction completion.

findings.impact: Software assumes the state change succeeded and may suppress future commands as redundant. A failed brightness or wake command can leave the physical panel out of sync with power/theme state, without a retained operation error or retry. Bitmap submission uses ESP_ERROR_CHECK, so error policy is inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Record each panel command result and actual acknowledgment, update applied state only on success, and add bounded retry/recovery with last failed operation/register.
findings.title: Panel command failures are ignored after host state is advanced
findings.trigger: An invert, brightness, sleep or wake DCS transaction returns an error.
findings.verification: Source review; no panel fault injection. Existing bitmap/rotation tests do not exercise DCS errors.

evidence.detail: Station intent is parked before timer creation.
esp_timer_create result is ignored.
Periodic start result is ignored, then on=1 and success are returned.
Auto-release only executes from the timer callback.

findings.impact: The station link is already parked and promiscuous mode enabled, but the function still marks the analyzer on and returns success. Without timer callbacks it cannot hop channels or enforce the 3-second auto-release contract; station reconnection requires a separate stop path.
findings.recommendation: Check timer creation/start, undo promiscuous mode and restore station intent on every failed entry, and keep an independent supervisor for lease expiry.
findings.title: Air analyzer reports success if its lease/hop timer fails
findings.trigger: Timer allocation or periodic start fails while entering the Wi-Fi air analyzer.
findings.verification: Source-proven failure path; host test suite has no analyzer timer fault injection.

evidence.detail: Loop captures now before earlier services and passes it to gps_service.
sentence obtains fresh ext_ms for fix acquisition.
Valid GGA records last_fix=now; RMC does so at line 167.
G_RUN pumps NMEA before checking freshness.
Uses old caller now minus new G->last_fix, with unsigned elapsed comparison.

findings.impact: sentence records a newer last_fix timestamp, but the post-pump stale check subtracts it from the older unsigned now. The elapsed value wraps and the same pass clears the newly valid fix. Physical frequency depends on task/I/O timing and has not been measured.
findings.recommendation: Refresh the monotonic timestamp after pump before stale checks, and use a wrap-safe elapsed helper that treats newer acquisition timestamps as fresh. Apply the same rule to lease and data timestamps across services.
findings.title: GPS can invalidate a newly parsed fix using the older service-loop timestamp
findings.trigger: gps_service receives now from loop entry, then pump parses a valid sentence at a later millisecond.
findings.verification: Exact source ordering and unsigned arithmetic reviewed; the extracted-helper renewal check demonstrates the same ordering class, but no GPS parser/hardware replay was performed.

evidence.detail: Clock command is found by substring search over the entire line.
Timezone command is also searched inside quoted content.
Any extracted time fields are applied before JSON handling.

findings.impact: The frame parser recognizes both the notification JSON and the text inside it as a clock command. svc applies the clock/timezone before posting the notification, potentially shifting alarms, dates and logs.
findings.recommendation: Parse top-level command framing lexically and ignore command-like strings inside JSON/quoted text. Add round-trip tests using benign notification examples and multiple framed commands.
findings.title: Notification text can be mistaken for a clock or timezone command
findings.trigger: A normal notification contains a documentation example such as setTime(...) or E.setTimeZone(...) within its quoted body.
findings.verification: Positive host regression against actual gb.c: checks/protocol/notification_clock.log. No phone or watch traffic was generated.

evidence.detail: Legacy GET maps any fopen failure to MISSING.
Paced GET has the same mapping.
CRC query also maps any fopen failure to MISSING.
Host treats MISSING as a missing file, not a transient transport/storage failure.

findings.impact: SDGET/SDGET2/SDCRC return MISSING; host raises FileNotFoundError and deliberately avoids retry. Operators cannot tell absence from the failure mode that blocked the previous flash.
findings.recommendation: Reserve MISSING for ENOENT; return a typed operation/error/errno response for other failures. Keep retries bounded and read-only; include SD generation and resource telemetry in failure reports.
findings.title: Storage read failures are reported as missing files
findings.trigger: fopen fails because of low DMA memory, exhausted handles, permission errors, or I/O errors rather than a nonexistent path.
findings.verification: Source-backed reachable condition. Prior flash evidence checkpoint-read-2.log includes unreadable slot 0 while allocation failures were occurring; do not infer permanent file absence from that message.

evidence.detail: Failed batches retain queue IDs specifically so replays can be identified.
bin_record accumulates every battery sample.
Async query deduplicates FOOD/WATER only.
Synchronous query has the same special case.

findings.impact: Intake records are deduplicated, but battery samples are counted twice, giving repeated samples extra weight and overstating sample counts. Offline exporters and on-watch summaries can disagree.
findings.recommendation: Deduplicate all journal records by durable identity before aggregation, or commit batches with durable replay-safe boundaries. Carry last-seen identity per stream where append ordering permits a bounded implementation.
findings.title: Retried journal records can bias on-watch battery-history averages
findings.trigger: A failed close/write batch already appended complete records, then retries the same boot/sequence IDs; battery-history query scans both copies.
findings.verification: Call-chain/code review; no new hardware reproduction. Existing recovered archives contain repeated records and exporters explicitly deduplicate them; a dedicated failed-close replay aggregation regression should be added.

evidence.detail: Generated test fixture provides do_get but no do_get2 stub.
Compile is asserted successful under Werror.
Current dispatcher references do_get2.

findings.impact: The intended mount/lease safety check does not exercise production code, leaving a storage regression blind spot despite other transfer tests passing.
findings.recommendation: Update the mock to include paced downloads and cover each early return/lease balance; run it in a single documented host validation command/CI gate.
findings.title: An SD lease regression test no longer compiles against the active transfer dispatcher
findings.trigger: Run tests/test_sd_asset_leases.py against the current recovered sources.
findings.verification: Audit check: 25 targeted existing tests, 24 passed and this one failed during compilation. checks/storage/existing-tests.log.

evidence.detail: Both BME280 and BMP280 chip IDs are accepted as EXT_ENV.
The BMP path supplies humidity=0.
LOCAL clamps the numeric humidity without checking a separate capability.
The resulting numeric value is labelled HUMIDITY percent.

findings.impact: The driver synthesizes humidity=0 for a chip without humidity sensing. The app presents a measured HUMIDITY 0% and an empty gauge instead of unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Add a humidity-valid/capability field to hal_env and show unavailable for BMP280 while retaining pressure and temperature support.
findings.title: An accepted BMP280 is shown as measuring zero percent humidity
findings.trigger: Use the explicitly supported BMP280 rather than the BME280, and view Barometer's LOCAL page.

verification.method: Inspected accepted chip IDs, compensation branch, and app draw path; no sensor hardware test.

evidence.detail: A reveal invokes enter with nos_revealed set.
Torch enter does not branch on reveal.
It resets mode=white and white level=1.0.
The next tick applies the reset level via the brightness override.

findings.impact: Torch's reveal enter is treated as a fresh visit, resetting mode to white and level to 100%. Its next tick requests full backlight, losing the user's chosen light on an ordinary interruption.
findings.recommendation: Preserve Torch's mode and per-mode level across covers/reveals, initialize defaults only on a new opening, and reapply the preserved override after the covering screen restores brightness.
findings.title: Revealing Torch after an alert resets red/dim mode to full white
findings.trigger: Select red Torch or lower the white light level, let a call/alarm/Find Watch cover the screen, and dismiss it.

verification.method: Checked engine cover/reveal callback semantics and Torch initialization/override path; panel output was not exercised.

evidence.detail: Generic logs record screen name/depth/reveal only.
Alarm matching, firing, timeout, and persistence path has no dedicated event/result log.
Timer actions likewise expose no structured action/state/result events.
Rejected GPS fixes have no counter/reason/event.
The coarse stop routine is emitted before final save completion is known.
Failure is retained only as an aggregate count rather than a request result.

findings.impact: Generic navigation records identify screen entry but not event generation, action request, backend completion, stale age, rejected point reason, or persistence outcome. Track/Recorder emit a coarse SP_ROUTINE value; LTE/audio expose aggregate debug counters, making a specific failure difficult to reconstruct.
findings.recommendation: Add bounded transition-only diagnostic events with request/session generation, old/new state, source, age/reason, and completion status. Rate-limit aggregate rejected-fix counters; keep message bodies/caller content out of routine logs.
findings.title: Critical time/connection actions lack result and transition diagnostics
findings.trigger: Investigate a missed alarm, nested alert, disappearing phone link, failed SMS, rejected GPS point, or Recorder save error after the fact.

verification.method: Reviewed log/printf/sports_emit call sites in every scoped app and the corresponding service/HAL paths.

evidence.detail: Ignore list includes build and firmware artifacts but no workspace worktree directory.
Named outputs share one object directory.
Verify output relies on ambient TEMP and fixed basename.
Existing GUID output pattern demonstrates a suitable local isolation approach.

findings.impact: .gitignore covers build/dist/firmware outputs but not .worktrees; git check-ignore returns no match for .worktrees/_audit_tmp/check.tmp. Build verification uses the ambient TEMP directory and fixed child name, and simulator named binaries share objects. An isolated audit/dev checkout can pollute status or place heavy temporary files on C:, and concurrent output provenance is unclear. This audit explicitly redirects TEMP/TMP to A: and writes checks separately.
findings.recommendation: Document and enforce workspace-local .worktrees plus A:-resident TEMP/TMP for heavy runs; ignore that private root, validate resolved output/delete targets and use GUID run directories or cache locks with manifests. Add disk-space/output-root preflight to heavy jobs.
findings.title: Private worktree and temporary-output policy is not encoded in repository tooling
findings.trigger: Create the required workspace-local .worktrees checkout/temp directory, then run status/add-all or concurrent simulator/test jobs with default settings.
findings.verification: git check-ignore .worktrees/_audit_tmp/check.tmp returned1/no match. No worktree or recursive move/delete was performed.

evidence.detail: Hardcoded COM3 and top-level port.open24.
Top-level try begins the active network/settings scenario.
Creates/connects a Windows WLAN profile.
Cleanup performs HardReset once original preferences exist, followed by UI restoration.

findings.impact: The module opens a hardcoded serial port at top level, then changes watch UI/preferences, joins a Windows WLAN profile and invokes HardReset during cleanup, even when an earlier assertion fails after original preferences were read. There is no CLI --port/identity/dry-run boundary or __main__ guard. Existing restoration logic is useful but cannot make import read-only or verify that COM3 is the intended watch.
findings.recommendation: Move execution into main(), require an explicit port and target identity, separate offline helpers from device scenarios, and describe the exact mutations/reset in --help. Keep restoration in a robust finally block and retain proof of the prior/current configuration.
findings.title: Connectivity hardware QA opens COM3 and performs mutations at module import
findings.trigger: Import tools/check_connectivity_device.py for helper discovery/testing, or execute it on a host where COM3 is a different target.
findings.verification: Source/AST-level review only. This module was not imported, executed, or allowed to access COM3.

evidence.detail: Navigation record carries hashed screen name,depth,revealing flag only.
Touch action record carries hashed screen name,event type,axis; no target coordinates/ID/result.
Button action similarly stores screen hash and event type.
Dismissal acts without a semantic diagnostic record of intended/current notification ID.
Toggle implements multiple distinct actions with no tile/value domain event.
Existing exporter builds name-ID decoding; avoid duplicating that capability.

findings.impact: Logs can identify a screen and input event, but cannot establish which card/tile/row/face was intended, which ID was acted on, or whether navigation completed/cancelled. This particularly obstructs diagnosing ENG-001. Screen-name hash decoding does exist in tools/diag_export.py, so the gap is payload semantics, not a missing decoder.
findings.recommendation: Emit sparse semantic records at action commit/completion with stable target ID and result, plus source/destination/transition outcome for navigation. Keep high-rate raw touch streams separate from these finite domain events.
findings.title: Generic action/navigation records cannot reconstruct selected UI targets or action completion
findings.trigger: Export diagnostics after a wrong action, interrupted transition, Control Center toggle, picker choice or notification dismissal.
findings.verification: Static producer/caller/exporter trace; no claim of dropped log transport. Validate by replaying a known card-dismiss and toggle sequence and resolving intent/result without screenshots.

evidence.detail: Header describes nos_dt as a whole number of frame periods; frame-run contract repeats quantization at line257.
Current implementation explicitly follows elapsed time, using elapsed_ms/1000 at line2241.
Ink-dim comment states dim-only changes are not repainted.
gfx_rec_cmd hashes fb->dim into the command signature.
Existing regression exercises irregular12/28/8/25ms intervals instead of quantized periods.

findings.impact: The header promises whole-period quantization and says ink dim is absent from damage hashes, whereas current implementation uses bounded exact elapsed dt and hashes dim. Implementers can introduce unnecessary manual markers or make incorrect timing assumptions.
findings.recommendation: Update nos.h to the exact bounded elapsed-time contract, distinguish authored frame sampling from engine dt, and document current dim tracking/callback requirements. Keep API documentation aligned with the current regression tests.
findings.title: Engine timing and ink-damage API comments describe superseded behavior
findings.trigger: Implement or debug a screen using the current nos.h contract, especially dt-dependent animation or a stationary ink-dim fade.
findings.verification: Direct header/implementation/test comparison; no behavior change or production edit performed.

evidence.detail: Line-up event is zeroed; mask/n are assigned but a remains0.
Line-up spokes correctly iterate mask.
All event kinds then circle S.px[e->a].

findings.impact: Line-up spokes correctly use the membership mask, but the final highlight ring uses zero-initialized a=0 (Mercury), producing a false planet emphasis.
findings.recommendation: Skip the single-planet ring for EV_LINEUP or deliberately highlight members from its mask.
findings.title: Line-up event highlight circles Mercury even when Mercury is not a member
findings.trigger: View a line-up event within1.5 days of its timestamp, with normal event lines enabled and rings closed.
findings.verification: Actual ep_events probe found line-up JD2451544.5 mask00f8, a0, Mercury absent; output in ephem-residual-repro.log. Raster implication is source-proven, not a screenshot observation.

evidence.detail: Script command accepts A/B and sets orrery_ring_plate.
Switch still described as temporary separate-return/status-capsule review switch.
Only use beyond definition is the scene key.
Final dock draw has no switch branch.

findings.impact: Both commands select the same final dock; a reviewer can mistake successful command acceptance/rebuild for a meaningful A/B visual test.
findings.recommendation: Remove or explicitly reject the obsolete selector, or implement/report the intended alternatives if they remain useful.
findings.title: Simulator ringplate A/B selector changes a cache key but has no rendering effect
findings.trigger: Use accepted simulator script command ringplate A or ringplate B for an Orrery plate comparison.
findings.verification: Repository search finds no rendering read of RING_PLATE/orrery_ring_plate, only definitions, script mutation and cache key.

evidence.detail: Default NOS_FPS is40; M_FPS follows it.
XF_HZ remains30.
Fade index uses elapsed seconds times XF_HZ.
Other face animation frames use M_FPS.
Blink uses fk_sec_k/M_FPS with old15/18 step thresholds.

findings.impact: The stated five-frame fade takes about seven40-Hz updates and repeats some perceptual levels instead of one level per nominal frame. The shared blink also retains30-fps phase constants, so its documented500ms hold is375ms at40Hz.
findings.recommendation: Use the configured cadence consistently for counted fades; express intended real-time blink milestones through named duration conversions if500ms is the product requirement.
findings.title: Shared date fades retain a30-Hz timebase under the configured40-Hz cadence
findings.trigger: A midnight/date-label change cross-fades on any ordinary face using fk_xfade with the default NOS_FPS40 build.
findings.verification: Source timebase comparison, not a physical judder claim. Card dt*30 rate scaling was separately noted but is not automatically classified as a malfunction.

evidence.detail: placement_source is a file-static initialized to PLACEMENT_USER.
configure_session freezes that volatile value into each workout.
Guided confirmation sets CALIBRATED; only the Sports manual toggle resets it at627.
Preferences persist hand selections and wrist_refs but no placement provenance/revision.
General Settings toggles wrist_left without informing the Sports placement_source flag.

findings.impact: Persisted wrist/gesture references survive, but placement_source resets to USER after reboot or can remain CALIBRATED after an unrelated manual wrist change. Later workout metadata can misstate how the chosen wrist was established.
findings.recommendation: Persist explicit wrist-selection source and calibration version with the selected wrist, or conservatively tag all subsequent manually selected sessions USER. Invalidate provenance consistently through a shared preference setter.
findings.title: Frozen wrist-placement provenance is only a volatile UI flag
findings.trigger: A guided wrist suggestion is confirmed and the system reboots, or the user subsequently changes watch wrist in general Settings rather than Sports setup.
findings.verification: Preference layout, both manual setters and guided setter traced. No claim that a guided suggestion establishes anatomical wrist identity; user confirmation remains required.

evidence.detail: HIST is64 samples.
Live samples are accepted when wall-clock delta>=50ms, then last resets to actual current time.
Ring increments once per accepted UI poll, not on a fixed producer clock.
Graph key is ACCEL +/-2G /4.3S; no acquisition timestamps are used in trace drawing at92-96.

findings.impact: At the nominal20Hz cap the ring holds about3.2seconds, while a30FPS UI commonly accepts a sample every66.7ms, about4.27seconds. Scheduling load can lengthen the span further; the fixed4.3S diagnostic label cannot establish a measured time axis.
findings.recommendation: Store sample timestamps and label the actual visible duration, or drive the live chart from a declared fixed-rate producer. Keep raw recorder rate/loss metadata separate from this filtered live preview.
findings.title: Live IMU graph advertises a fixed4.3-second window without timestamped sampling
findings.trigger: The live graph fills its64-entry ring. It samples when at least50ms have passed, with no timestamps attached to individual entries.
findings.verification: Source arithmetic and scheduling dependence inspected. No claim that raw recorder runs at the UI rate; its separate recorder is reviewed by root.

evidence.detail: HR quality/range/age gates collapse into ok=false and zero live HR at300; no retained per-reason counts.
GPS exposes a few broad states; jump/finite/range reasons at354/384 are not separately counted.
Invalid or implausible samples reset boundaries without reason counters.

findings.impact: Coverage totals and coarse GPS state show that data is missing, but not which age, quality, saturation, discontinuity or I/O condition caused it. findings.recommendation: Add bounded per-session rejection counters, latest failure time/reason and accepted acquisition times. Capture storage operation/slot/errno and worker resource failure separately; persist summaries when storage recovers without flooding sample logs.
findings.title: Workout quality rejection and writer failures lack retained causal detail
findings.trigger: A workout loses HR/GNSS/motion coverage or a checkpoint fails, and the developer later inspects only stored snapshots/status.
findings.verification: Logging callsites and all quality/error returns inspected. This is an explicit observability gap, not evidence that any specific physical session failed for one of these reasons.

evidence.detail: Persistent store comment still describes device NVS, while active implementation is SD-authoritative.
Advertises serial ota URL/ota sd; active nos_main command dispatch has no corresponding calls.
Generic BOARD record prints audio=0 unconditionally.
Weak display override alone updates s_display_mode; active NOS strong hal_display_power bypasses it.
C board explicitly rejected, despite comment referring to a legacy-main fallback not selected by current CMake.

findings.impact: NVS-only storage comments, retired serial OTA instructions, a hardcoded board audio=0, and an ext display_mode cache that the strong NOS override never updates obscure the current implementation. findings.recommendation: Update comments/help to the active source of truth; expose supported base/strap capabilities and current applied display/radio state in one versioned snapshot. Mark dormant entrypoints and legacy code clearly.
findings.title: Legacy contracts and diagnostic labels misdescribe current hardware and storage behavior

limitations: This is a targeted, read-only source audit of the current recovered dirty workspace, not a proof of absence of defects. No implementation fixes or new firmware build/flash were performed.

All 26 launcher entries, 70 production screen definitions and 129 compiled production translation units have coverage associations. File/entrypoint coverage does not imply every branch or screen was dynamically exercised.

Generated tables/fonts/art were reviewed as data, indexing, ownership and compatibility contracts, not individually verified literal values. Inactive core/apps and firmware/main/main.c are not the active OS.
ESP-IDF/FreeRTOS/vendor dependencies are reviewed through the project contracts and configuration used here, not as separate exhaustive audits of dependency source trees.

Host tests and injected positive repros validate narrow software behavior. Optional hardware, real phone protocols, unplugged battery endurance, physical sensor accuracy and power-loss/media-removal resilience remain unverified.

A fresh read-only USB diagnostic snapshot has no current allocation/SD log errors. Earlier low-DMA storage failures and two crash boots are separate historical evidence; exact crash causation is not established.
The live preference hash/brightness changed since the prior flash by user interaction (current 6f530340 / 62). The audit did not restore older settings. No device mutation was used for verification.
The branch HEAD predates recovered work; this report uses inventoried current files. No worktree was created or firmware substituted. All new audit/temp artifacts reside on A:.

Priority expresses engineering urgency for this early-stage system. P0 means demonstrated critical emergency (none confirmed); P1 means address before trusting data/update boundaries; P2 means functional/reliability improvement; P3 means lower-impact correctness/documentation/observability debt.

logging_plan.detail: Versioned bounded binary records: monotonic timestamp, optional UTC plus validity, boot/reset ID, sequence, build/ELF/source IDs, subsystem, severity, event ID, action/session/request ID, state before/after, result/error, duration and explicit evidence-loss counters. Keep human formatting and symbol resolution on the host.

logging_plan.detail: Keep panic-safe/RTC/internal evidence for reset reason, task/core, fault PC, stack/backtrace or coredump reference, last action/session and allocation request/caps/callsite token with internal/DMA free/largest/minimum. Use safe capture hooks and deferred persistence. Preserve matching ELF and a host symbolizer; do not do file I/O or formatted logging inside unsafe hooks.
logging_plan.title: Crash and allocation first-fault channel

logging_plan.detail: Trace lease acquisition, mount generation, lock wait, operation phase, stable path ID, errno/result, bytes, slot/generation/CRC, queue high-water/drop, dirty age, fsync/readback latency and retry outcome. Log CSV chunk/checkpoint/recovery boundaries, not every IMU sample. Give critical faults a separate reserved budget from regular sensor history.
logging_plan.title: Storage phase and recovery trace

logging_plan.detail: Record every power state transition with reason, SOC validity/source, rail sample age, CPU/APB lock owners and held duration, display/brightness, actual radio/strap state, wake source, sleep refusal and recorder/background owners. Summarize periodic residency. A measured current/charge integration run with known battery/USB state is required before claiming consumption or capacity.
logging_plan.title: Power ownership and measured evidence

logging_plan.detail: Begin/result events with stable target IDs for settings changes, alarms/timers, notifications, SMS, memos, workout start/pause/save/recover and sensor calibration. Include sample timestamp/quality/stale reason, source, worn wrist and playing hand/confidence/provenance. Log presentation and acquisition separately to detect stale UI.
logging_plan.title: App actions and sensor truth

logging_plan.detail: Use a bounded triggerable frame ring for input-to-present, tick/layout/raster/blur, DMA submit/complete/wait, asset admission/publish/cancel and SD stalls. Capture configuration, moving regions, cache cold/warm, missed floor/deadline and relevant lock/resource owners. Aggregate normal frames; preserve a short pre/post fault window.
logging_plan.title: Frame and asynchronous work spans

logging_plan.detail: Per-module levels with bounded duration, rate limiting/coalescing, queue/drop telemetry and explicit session markers. Export one manifest-linked redacted bundle with logs, settings schema/hash, sensor/profile metadata, trace, crash and matching build artifacts. Default to excluding credentials, phone message text, raw contacts and location; make sensitive data selection explicit.
logging_plan.title: Retention, export and developer controls

BLE transfer polling runs synchronously on cmd task using BLE_IO. USB raw transfer reads occur synchronously on that same task, so no simultaneous ordinary USB parser read is shown.
Driver takes up to requested BYTEBUF length, copies bytes to caller buffer before vRingbufferReturnItem, and returns zero if no data. No ordinary zero-fill path found.
ISR reads only counted FIFO bytes, then ignores xRingbufferSendFromISR return. Buffer-full loss is a plausible unobserved loss mechanism; loss alone does not create NUL from purely nonzero input.
Ring item return takes the ringbuffer critical section. No retained item pointer survives the driver copy; cross-core task migration alone is not proof of invalid ownership.

changes.detail: Reviewed root's two persistent staging/published PSRAM buffers, mutex-serialized HTTP/BLE writers and reader counts. Newly allocated pointer publication now shares the reader lock (allocation stays outside it). Legacy raw accessor also acquires a pin instead of returning an already-released pointer; every accessor requires release.

Enforce BLE connection ownership and the 15-second idle lease on every chunk/commit. Reject zero-byte data chunks, incomplete commits, extra commit bytes, out-of-order/overflowing offsets and malformed mbufs without publishing. A different connection cannot hijack a live writer.

Retain exact 125000-byte preallocation length rejection and staged publication; cap each receive at min(4096, remaining), check receive result and deadline after blocking receive. Prior pixels/generation survive every failed transfer.

Actual complete HAL source exercises length values through SIZE_MAX without allocation/read, first/second-buffer allocation faults, truncation/stall/over-report, BLE framing/ownership/leases/commits, simultaneous old/new pins, writer mutex exclusion and allocation canaries.

changes.detail: Publish IMU/file, preference loading/dirty, workout and track admission policy on the UI thread under a short spinlock. HTTP tasks no longer read UI-owned workout/preferences directly. Default/unrefreshed policy fails closed; a claim needs a <=2-second-old snapshot. A later blocked snapshot aborts an active transfer.

Atomic single-writer claim binds to the original setup-session generation and a 180-second transfer deadline. Token validation is before body allocation/read/task launch. Ending/reopening Phone setup cannot revive a writer. ota_busy stays claimed through boot selection/reply/reboot.

Host mutation owner=2 competes atomically with OTA writer owner=1. A paired end publishes the resulting admission policy before releasing to owner=0, closing a check-busy-then-start race. Writer cleanup can only release its own owner=1; render/read-only work remains permitted.

Track successful esp_ota_begin ownership explicitly; abort only an owned open handle. esp_ota_end consumes its handle even on error. Recheck authorization after validation and before boot selection. Failed begin cannot abort an invalid handle.

Reject a successful begin with NULL handle; never perform/finish without a valid begin. Incremental perform checks generation/deadline, rejects incomplete data, handles expiry before finish as timeout, and calls exactly one finish or abort. Do not print private URLs.

HTTP raw URL bodies reject embedded NUL, control, whitespace and trailing garbage bytes. Public URL API has a bounded 512-byte absolute HTTP(S) URL contract; queued tasks revalidate their original writer lease.

SD keeps a mounted lease for the operation. Each bounded read opens/seeks/length-checks/reads/closes its descriptor under one short SD lock; no descriptor survives a lock timeout and no unbounded cleanup-lock retry remains. Check ferror/fclose and image capacity before opening a flash sink. SDK validation remains the final image check; rename failure retains update.bin.
Only log confirmation if esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback succeeds.

Actual complete ota.c exercises concurrent pthread CAS claims, all entrypoint authorization, stale/generation/dirty/loading/activity policy, HTTP memory/task/async/read/start/write/end faults, URL null/start/perform/incomplete/finish/expiry/deadline/NUL faults, and SD lease/lock/open/seek/read/close/size/write faults. Use worst adjacent painted-completion interval to select the owner. Nested record/raster/history/layer timers and overlapping cores cannot simply be added or subtracted as exclusive CPU times.

Hard30FPS floor remains required; do not lower quality, disable blur, skip frames/features or enlarge scarce internal/DMA buffers to manufacture a pass.

already_present_not_new_optimizations: Native prepared row leaves already precompute weights, specialize absent levels/zero phase, and move X-span sorting out of per-row loops; preserve the nested 64-step then Q16 rounding.

Settings already publishes entry signatures/geometry once per frame, compact control atlas, bounded carry state and ROM rows. Native history copy and packed/uniform history shortcuts already exist; treating them as future fixes would duplicate current work.

Paired rotation stores are already active. Canonical 16-row raster plus 8-row DMA chunks is an internal-RAM tradeoff; increasing buffers would consume scarce internal/DMA memory and is not a low-risk default recommendation.

New OTA admission uses cached owner snapshots and short locks; new logging is sparse. diag_log_tick power/heap summaries run every30s and nos_heap_diag_tick heap census every1s. No source evidence supports blaming a per-frame filesystem logger or removing admission/fault evidence to meet the budget.
build/alpha05/results/performance_review.conclusion: First test the root-qualified physical image. If it misses, exact launcher curve reuse is the best proven low-risk source candidate from this review; duplicate Settings ROM sync is secondary. Per-frame continuous blur remains unqualified until eligibility and final-visible applied mechanisms can be reconciled without overlap or unknown coverage. No production/tool/test edit was made during this review.

minimal_proposal.independent_denominator: Freeze app/semantic owner, source revision, before/after authored pose, elapsed interval, held-policy and requested exposure at tick. Derive eligible visible moving requests independently of successful cache/filter decisions; do not define eligibility as 'filter ran' or as painted alone. In the required benchmark, a blur-disabled policy/configuration invalidates the window rather than exempting movement.
minimal_proposal.limit: This can prove declared engine coverage without overlap inflation. It remains distinct from optical blur appearance and whether the unchanged normalized density/box/EMA approximations meet the user's visual requirement. It must not force lower density, shorter trails, omitted features, altered preferences or skipped frames.
minimal_proposal.mechanism_histogram: Use a 4-bit mask NATIVE=1,LIVE=2,GENERIC_CACHE=4,TEMPORAL=8 and a 16-bin histogram per frame status, so a native+history frame enters only mask9 once. Inclusive mechanism counters can remain diagnostics, but their sums are not covered-frame counts. Unique covered area is a set union; if source kinds overlap retain provenance rather than arbitrarily counting one twice.
minimal_proposal.mutually_exclusive_frame_status: After the existing exposure/DMA fence, each moving frame is exactly COVERED, GAP or UNKNOWN. COVERED requires zero uncovered eligible area and no unknown source/ownership. Gap reason and first frame/owner are retained in bounded fields. An eligible moving frame with no paint is separate NO_PRESENT/GAP, not removed by the consecutive-painted population.
minimal_proposal.raster_receipts: After clipping, producers report typed native-prepared, live-spatial and generic-cache receipts with stable owner/revision plus the actual kernel/levels/weights used. Include source-not-ready, invalid, clipped-empty and budget-rejected outcomes. Distinguish sharp/pose-only work from non-identity exposure; a blurred flag is insufficient. History receipts need valid previous sharp data, enabled exposure and non-identity weights; first seed/copy is not temporal exposure. Equal-valued pixels with valid enabled history may be equivalent covered work.
minimal_proposal.scope: Minimum useful quiet instrumentation for current Apps/Settings; declaring all animations/faces covered additionally requires their actual moving-owner request metadata. No target-wide claim can be inferred from two menus.
minimal_proposal.small_summary: Expose eligible_moving_frames, eligible_no_present, covered_frames, gap_frames, unknown_frames, unique_required/covered/uncovered area, admission rejection reasons and bounded first/worst gap identity. Version the new capture schema; old/absent fields fail closed for per-frame blur qualification. Keep output outside the quiet capture and retain exact ELF/source identity. Do not log app content, health samples, credentials or locations.
minimal_proposal.unique_coverage: At final stripe composition, intersect required motion regions with the final visible ownership and union native/live/cache receipts. Temporal history covers only the complementary regions where it has valid prior data. Reuse the existing span/coverage/exclusion flow, adding mechanism provenance; do not add processed-area totals. A later foreground overwrite or exclusion must retire an earlier receipt. Use a bounded captured span/region ledger or tracked PSRAM scratch only while capture is active; overflow, source-generation mismatch or insufficient final-ownership information yields UNKNOWN, never success.

coverage_observability.specific_acceptance_gap: capture_statistics currently accepts any positive v_filter_frames, blend_frames or generic blurred_frames in a window. This proves some blur, not every eligible moving frame or region. Native prepared work is not directly reported. Budget admission can reject live spatial blur, with temporal history potentially covering the complementary area. No new sharp-frame defect is inferred from aggregate zeros/positives alone.

BLE empty polling reserves a bounded208-byte frame but no data buffer is filled unless a BLE command is queued. Essential command task stack6144 is dynamically allocated internally via FreeRTOS. Stack canary checks enabled; compiler stack protector and heap poisoning disabled. No cmd high-water measurement is currently included in info; NOSUISTACK is the UI task.

SDK ISR reads at most64 bytes from counted RX FIFO into its bounded local buffer, then sends exactly that count to RX BYTEBUF. Send failure is currently ignored, so overflow loss is unobserved. Task read returns0 on absent data, otherwise copies ring bytes into destination before returning the item. No zero-fill or timeout-to-NUL branch found.

BYTEBUF allocation is separate control calloc plus exact malloc4096 storage, not an8192-plus-header allocation.4096 is internal-preferred under current threshold, and allocation occurs before optional radios. Generic default allocator can fall back if preferred internal allocation fails; actual runtime memory class is not proven by the threshold. No RX buffer PSRAM-placement conclusion is justified without classification.

BYTEBUF disallows a second outstanding retrieval and keeps the item unfree until driver copies it and returns it. Ring state changes use critical-section locking. Task migration does not by itself establish a returned-buffer ownership race; no such race was identified.

S3 FIFO rdwr_byte is explicitly32bits to avoid read-modify-write. Current compiled ISR and no-driver VFS TX perform plain stores to EP1, not accidental RX reads. After VFS use_driver, both console TX and fsync route through driver/driver-wait with locks. No active production switch back or ordinary stdin reader was found. Early boot console is direct TX until use_driver; driver RX intentionally preserves already-present FIFO data. Residual input at startup remains unmeasured.

Current power policy has min80/max240 and light_sleep=false; tickless idle is off. S3 clock source maps both80 and240 to the same480MHz PLL, with divider change on the fast path. SOF monitoring can report false/disconnected and make VFS suppress TX, but no reviewed path converts received characters toNUL. APB/clock/affinity/radio causation is unproven.

Ordinary host temporary-bytes lifetime is inconsistent with the configured blocking path: SerialLines.write owns data through serial.write and flush; pyserial to_bytes returns the same bytes; pyserial write keeps local data through GetOverlappedResult(bWait=True) for positive write_timeout. Exact installed CPython3.12.10 c_void_p bytes converter retains the original PyBytes data pointer/reference, with no transient copied buffer. Initial NUL is length-counted by WriteFile, not C-string truncated. write_timeout0 uses a different async branch and is not the configured benchmark path. This does not prove that the Windows USB stack or underlying driver obeys every completion guarantee.

No concrete heap/DMA out-of-bounds writer or parser defect was identified by this scoped source review. Lack of a canary panic does not exclude heap, pointer, ISR-stack, or local-state corruption. WiFi retry messages and active-vs-idle probe association do not establish causation.
